Append one helper operation per shell call. Use native\\nWrite/Edit for files; read with native Read or the documented `read-text` helper.\\nPrefer one `read-text` call for independent files whose exact paths are known.\\nKeep normal permissions: no wrappers, loops, pipes,\\ndirectory listing, direct client commands or permission changes. This index\\ndescribes capabilities; it supplies no workflow or finished artifact.\\n\\n## Draft mutations\\n\\nPrefer typed input for the operations below. This table supplies their CLI fields;\\nyou do not also need their raw schemas or help files unless a needed field is\\nmissing. Choose the operation, target, versions, key and content yourself.\\n\\n```text\\nremote OPERATION --typed --compact --record ABSOLUTE_NEW_RECORD [FIELDS]\\n```\\n\\nEvery typed mutation takes `--operation-key KEY --expected-project-version N\\n--evaluator-file FILE`. Use the selected `evaluator_file` path. The fixed adapter\\nsupplies the selected endpoint/project/token environment and exact installed\\nclient wheel. The client constructs the existing request and verifies its identity.\\n\\n| Operation | Other fields |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| `import` | `--source-manifest FILE`; use selected `source_manifest` |\\n| `draft-open` | `--baseline ID --work-order WO-ID` |\\n| `create-artifact` | `--context UUID --context-version N --domain NAME --artifact-type TYPE`; optional `--artifact ID --include-document` |\\n| `revise-artifact` | `--context UUID --context-version N --artifact ID --expected-revision REVISION --document-file FILE` |\\n\\nHosted `create-artifact` allocates the ID and writes the draft in one operation.\\nIt has no `--dry-run` option; the local repository preview command does not apply.\\n\\nThe client never refreshes a version or retries a mutation on its own. Typed and\\nraw input cannot be mixed. Documents are exact UTF-8 files. No manual base64 or\\ncopied client digest is needed. `--include-document` adds one read of the exact\\ncreated revision, returning text or a decoded file path. Inspect it before editing.\\n\\n`--record` retains the command. Its new `.evidence` directory retains exact\\nrequests/responses and decoded documents. The displayed `client_view` is the\\nclient's own view. Inspect outcomes and findings; read required omitted content.\\nDo not reread a whole receipt just to extract a small field already displayed.\\nA capture error after send can leave a committed effect. Reconcile its original\\nkey with `remote operation --key KEY --record ABSOLUTE_NEW_RECORD`.\\n\\n## Read one revision\\n\\n```text\\nremote read --typed --compact --record ABSOLUTE_NEW_RECORD --artifact ID --expected-revision REVISION --context UUID --context-version N\\n```\\n\\nFor an imported baseline, replace the context fields with `--baseline ID`.\\nReads take no `--operation-key`, `--expected-project-version` or `--evaluator-file`.\\nChoose the exact revision and context from the selected inputs or actual results.\\n\\n## Reads and discovery\\n\\n| Need | Operation |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| Service readiness and selected components | `remote status --record ABSOLUTE_NEW_RECORD` |\\n| Local wheel metadata | `identity` |\\n| Captured calls, reads and failures so far | `observations --record ABSOLUTE_NEW_RECORD`; retains the full snapshot and returns its field pointers, no content verdict |\\n| Complete released instruction sections | `instructions --section \\\"RESOURCE_ID#HEADING\\\"`; repeat for up to 12 sections |\\n| One unknown input location | `find-file BASENAME --under RELATIVE_DIRECTORY/` |\\n| One exact inventory entry | `lookup-file RELATIVE_NAME` |\\n| One saved JSON field | `read-json ABSOLUTE_FILE --pointer '\\\"/field\\\"'`; omit pointer for root; optional `--keys` |\\n| A raw base64 field | Add `--decode-base64` to that field read |\\n| One text file or independent reads together | `read-text ABSOLUTE_FILE [ABSOLUTE_FILE ...]`; up to eight selected inventoried inputs, the launcher-pinned task.md, or work files, at most 64 KiB output |\\n| Recover a truncated text read | `read-text ABSOLUTE_FILE --offset 0 --limit 4096`; one file, character offsets; continue from next_offset until complete is true |\\n\\nFor `instructions`, use canonical IDs such as `docs/engineering/harness/DRAFT_DEFINITIONS.md#read-this-when`. The earlier `released-resources/` inventory prefix also works. Request known sections together.\\nFor authoring checklists and the repeated released 0.22.1 continuation heading,\\nuse the exact selectors in the selected plugin's `change/references/hosted-drafts.md`.\\n\\nFor known paths, use them directly. Inventory names are relative to the staged\\ninputs directory: `released-resources/docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md`,\\n`source/src/greeting.py`, `client-help/create-artifact.txt`. **Do not add `inputs/`\\nto these names.** Native Read takes the absolute path, not an inventory name.\\nA digest or lookup is not a content read. Batch independent reads when their exact\\npaths are known. Unknown headings must not be guessed;\\nread the named file once to locate its actual headings. Request known current\\nsections together and reuse unchanged content. A full inventory is not required.\\n\\nSource inspection and test execution are different actions. Drafting a verification\\ncontract describes future checks; it does not require running them. If the task\\nauthorizes execution, use [Execution tools](native-execution-tools.md).\\n\\n## Other operations\\n\\nRaw mode remains `remote OPERATION --request ABSOLUTE_FILE --record ABSOLUTE_NEW_RECORD`.\\nUse it for operations without typed input, or when explicitly checking a raw\\ncontract. Original schemas are under `reference/server/contracts/`. Selected\\nschema views use `schemas/remote-v1/OPERATION.json` or `schemas/read-v1/OPERATION.json`.\\nEach view retains its original pointer/digest. Lifecycle test-copy schemas are\\nseparate; do not load them for drafting alone. `--key` reads a receipt, not a document.\\n\\nFor lifecycle rehearsal use `remote rehearse --request ABSOLUTE_FILE --record\\nABSOLUTE_NEW_RECORD`. The helper supplies the direct client's `--test-copy` flag;\\ndo not add that flag yourself. The request still needs `test_copy: true`.\\nThe selected plugin's `change/references/hosted-test-lifecycle.md` provides exact\\nreleased section selectors and pointers to individual action schemas.\\nFor a handoff file, `encode-file ABSOLUTE_FILE` returns its actual byte count,\\nSHA-256 and base64 content. It takes no output flag. Copy those returned values\\nunchanged; do not compute or guess a replacement digest.\\n\\nUse `observations --record ABSOLUTE_NEW_RECORD` before the final report. Read its\\nselected fields as needed. `observed_content_reads` contains successful visible\\nread metadata; `file_reads` retains Claude Read attempts, including failures.\\nUse the observed trace instead of rebuilding it with inventory lookups. Missing\\nreads remain unknown; rereading now does not prove an earlier read. The capture\\nmay be incomplete, and subsequent report writes are not yet counted. Keep the\\nrecord path as evidence instead of copying every command. This supplies no draft\\ntext, content judgement or lifecycle decision.\\n\\n`command_records` includes extensionless record names. Each row points to its\\noriginal capture and copies selected exact `response_fields`, including available\\nreceipt, outcome and provenance values. Rows are sorted by filename, not time.\\nUse an indexed row to locate evidence, then inspect its original request/result\\nfor the claim. The index does not select a handoff base or certify a retry.\\n\\nRetain failed calls and recoveries. Template admission is not a content review.\\nReport only inspected facts and actual outcomes; distinguish unresolved content\\nfrom a completed definition. Do not claim an exhaustive failure count from memory.\\n\"}\r\n",

Before links, read [DEFINITION_LINKS.md#links-between-definitions](DEFINITION_LINKS.md#links-between-definitions). Before authoring, read [../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#design-simplicity](../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#design-simplicity) and the exact type checklist linked in this file.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"fef13ff697eca3188c35b224644f1baf22534d9cb30142f440882d170d28bc6c\"}, {\"heading\": \"draft-any-missing-definitions\", \"title\": \"Draft any missing definitions\", \"anchor\": \"draft-any-missing-definitions\", \"start_line\": 29, \"end_line\": 108, \"content\": \"### Draft any missing definitions\\n\\n**Inputs:** The confirmed outcome, scope limits, and missing-definition list\\nfrom [Identify the existing artifacts that apply to the change](DEFINE_CHANGE.md#identify-the-existing-artifacts-that-apply-to-the-change).\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** New drafts of the missing intents (INT), capabilities\\n  (CAP), requirements (REQ), specifications (SPEC), applicable architectures\\n  (ARCH), and required architecture decisions (ADR). None if no definitions\\n  are missing.\\n- **Domain files and directories:** The structure reported by\\n  `scaffold-domain`, created only if the selected domain is missing.\\n- **Transient working material:** The inventory updated with generated IDs\\n  and file paths. Retain it under the same conditions as [Describe the intended outcome](DEFINE_CHANGE.md#describe-the-intended-outcome).\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Read `Design simplicity` in `docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md`.\\n2. Select the domain for each missing definition from the inventory. For a\\n   missing domain, preview its creation with the domain commands below.\\n3. Inspect the proposed domain paths. Resolve any reported conflict before\\n   running the domain creation command.\\n4. Select the first missing artifact type from the table below. Skip types\\n   already covered by unchanged existing artifacts.\\n5. Run the artifact preview command. Inspect its type, destination path, and\\n   `allocated_id`.\\n6. Run the artifact creation command with that exact ID. If a conflict occurs,\\n   repeat the preview; do not overwrite an existing record.\\n7. Open the returned file. Complete its title, owners, dates, content, and\\n   declared links. Replace all template placeholders.\\n8. Apply `### Checklist` under the matching `## TYPE` heading in\\n   `docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md`.\\n9. Read the completed draft. Record its ID and path in the inventory.\\n10. Repeat actions 4\\u20139 for each remaining missing definition.\\n\\n| Order | Artifact | TYPE | Content | Declared links |\\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\\n| 1 | Intent (INT) | `intent` | Problem, intended outcome, affected users, and scope limits. | None required here. |\\n| 2 | Capability (CAP) | `capability` | The ability needed to achieve the outcome. | `derives_from` \\u2192 intent (INT). |\\n| 3 | Requirement (REQ) | `requirement` | Observable behavior, conditions, and acceptance criteria. | `derives_from` \\u2192 capability (CAP). |\\n| 4 | Specification (SPEC) | `specification` | Detailed behavior, constraints, failure behavior, and checkable examples. | `specifies` \\u2192 requirement (REQ). |\\n| 5 | Architecture (ARCH), when applicable | `architecture` | Components, boundaries, and the architecture decision assessment. | `addresses` \\u2192 requirement (REQ); `conforms_to` \\u2192 specification (SPEC). |\\n| 6 | Architecture decision (ADR), when required | `adr` | Context, alternatives, chosen design, and consequences. | `decides` \\u2192 architecture (ARCH). |\\n\\nRecord an unresolved design choice for [Record unresolved decisions (DEC)](RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md#record-unresolved-decisions-dec). Do not present a recommendation\\nas an agreed architecture decision (ADR). Prepare verification contracts (VER)\\nin [Define how the result will be verified](DRAFT_DEFINITIONS.md#define-how-the-result-will-be-verified).\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\nFor a missing domain, use the first command in action 2 and the second only\\nafter reviewing the preview in action 3:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl scaffold-domain REPO --domain DOMAIN --dry-run --json\\nharnessctl scaffold-domain REPO --domain DOMAIN --json\\n```\\n\\nFor each missing artifact, use this **creation sequence** in actions 5\\u20136.\\nReplace `TYPE` with the table value. Replace `ARTIFACT-ID` in the second\\ncommand with the first command's `allocated_id`:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl create-artifact REPO --domain DOMAIN --type TYPE --dry-run --json\\nharnessctl create-artifact REPO --domain DOMAIN --type TYPE --id ARTIFACT-ID --json\\n```\\n\\nThe preview writes nothing and does not reserve an ID. Creation writes one\\nincomplete template and returns its path. Content completion is a separate\\nediting action. The JSON output does not contain the authoring checklist.\\n\\n**Completion:** Each missing definition has a completed draft with an ID and\\npath. Unresolved choices are identified. If no definitions are missing,\\nrecord `None needed` in the transient inventory.\\n\\n**Later use:** These definitions supply the verification contracts (VER) in\\n[Define how the result will be verified](DRAFT_DEFINITIONS.md#define-how-the-result-will-be-verified) and the governing links in work orders (WO) in [Prepare work orders (WO) linking the definitions, scope, planned work, and verification requirements](DRAFT_WORK_ORDERS.md#prepare-work-orders-wo-linking-the-definitions-scope-planned-work-and-verification-requirements). Their acceptance\\nis handled in the authorization process.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"c38865671a81429dd291d9f9bb333deae02a4098d4afcf034f293ee919e990e0\"}, {\"heading\": \"define-how-the-result-will-be-verified\", \"title\": \"Define how the result will be verified\", \"anchor\": \"define-how-the-result-will-be-verified\", \"start_line\": 109, \"end_line\": 165, \"content\": \"### Define how the result will be verified\\n\\n**Inputs:** The selected requirements (REQ), specifications (SPEC), proposed\\namendments, and existing verification contracts (VER).\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** New or updated verification contracts (VER) in\\n  `draft` where coverage is missing. None created or modified where existing\\n  contracts provide unchanged coverage. Accepted contracts remain unchanged.\\n- **Transient working material:** The selection of reused verification\\n  contracts (VER), any amendment proposals prepared through [Propose any needed amendments to existing definitions](AMEND_DEFINITIONS.md#propose-any-needed-amendments-to-existing-definitions), coverage\\n  gaps, and unresolved questions. Retain these under the same conditions\\n  as [Describe the intended outcome](DEFINE_CHANGE.md#describe-the-intended-outcome).\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Read each selected requirement's (REQ) acceptance criteria and linked\\n   specifications (SPEC).\\n2. Compare those criteria with the existing verification contracts (VER).\\n3. Select unchanged contracts that cover the proposed behavior.\\n4. For each coverage gap, create a verification contract (VER) with the\\n   commands below, or use [Propose any needed amendments to existing definitions](AMEND_DEFINITIONS.md#propose-any-needed-amendments-to-existing-definitions) to propose an amendment to an existing one.\\n5. Complete `Requirement-to-evidence matrix`. For each requirement (REQ),\\n   record its ID, method, case or evidence, and pass condition. Use `test`,\\n   `analysis`, `inspection`, or `demonstration` as the method.\\n6. Specify the inputs, platform, evaluator, and command or manual actions for\\n   each check. Derive expected results from the requirement (REQ) and\\n   specification (SPEC), not from candidate output.\\n7. Set `[relations].verifies` to the covered requirement (REQ) IDs.\\n8. Complete `Independence`, `Evidence retention`, and applicable assessment\\n   sections in each new or edited draft.\\n9. Apply `## verification` \\u2192 `### Checklist` in\\n   `docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md`.\\n10. Retain questions about missing criteria or methods for [Record unresolved decisions (DEC)](RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md#record-unresolved-decisions-dec).\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\nFor each new verification contract (VER), run the creation sequence from\\n[Draft any missing definitions](DRAFT_DEFINITIONS.md#draft-any-missing-definitions) with these arguments. Inspect the preview before creation; replace\\n`VER-ID` with its `allocated_id`:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl create-artifact REPO --domain DOMAIN --type verification --dry-run --json\\nharnessctl create-artifact REPO --domain DOMAIN --type verification --id VER-ID --json\\n```\\n\\nNo harness command writes the verification method or pass criteria. The human\\nor agent completes that content. No verification record (VREC) is created here.\\n\\n**Completion:** Every selected requirement (REQ) has a defined verification\\nmethod and pass condition, or an explicit unresolved question. Each proposed\\ncheck identifies how to perform it and where its evidence will be retained.\\n\\n**Later use:** [Prepare work orders (WO) linking the definitions, scope, planned work, and verification requirements](DRAFT_WORK_ORDERS.md#prepare-work-orders-wo-linking-the-definitions-scope-planned-work-and-verification-requirements) links these contracts to work orders (WO). The execution\\nand verification processes later perform the checks and assess the evidence.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"16a9ea7323450e244b26edd2d1ad757048124b627bcfffa157c8b173f57f363c\"}]}, {\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\hag-context-correction34-20261011\\\\codex-291\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"71de2cc92a470e2da25d525e3ad002b77faedb6ef0e69e2fa476a2fa4cb78ff5\", \"bytes\": 11691, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"design-simplicity\", \"title\": \"Design simplicity\", \"anchor\": \"design-simplicity\", \"start_line\": 21, \"end_line\": 58, \"content\": \"## Design simplicity\\n\\nFor unfinished work, `harnessctl validate-draft REPO --artifact ID --json`\\nreports whether one supported draft has an admissible shape. Only exact values\\nat the same type and field in this evaluator's canonical template, and missing\\nor empty required authoring links, can be reported as incomplete. Invalid\\nidentity, dates, metadata shapes, actual endpoints, lifecycle history and\\ndisposition are errors. A missing non-template ID is an error. Background\\nfindings remain visible; this result makes no whole-repository validity claim.\\nComplete the authoring checklist and pass ordinary approval gates before\\nrequesting approval. Draft admission grants no authority to write or approve.\\n\\nChoose the least complex design that satisfies the agreed requirements and\\nconstraints. Justify material added complexity by the need it serves and why\\na simpler approach is insufficient. Consider the effort to understand, build,\\ntest, operate and change the whole solution. Defer speculative needs. Review\\nboth the necessity of the specified behavior and the simplicity of its\\nimplementation. Preserve correctness and the project's required quality and\\nsafety properties.\\n\\nStart from the smallest complete solution. Each project supplies its agreed\\nusers, scale, operating conditions and quality constraints. Agreed future needs\\ncan matter; imagined flexibility alone is insufficient. Credible risk analysis\\ncan justify prevention before an incident. Fewer lines, shorter specifications\\nor fewer tests do not establish simplicity; moving work to users, operations\\nor dependencies also has a cost.\\n\\nApply the relevant questions below before definition approval and during design\\nand implementation review. Return unjustified obligations or design complexity\\nfor revision through the existing decision process. Explain material choices\\nin the existing specification, design or review: the need, why a simpler option\\nis insufficient and the added cost. Scale the explanation to the decision; a\\nsmall choice may need one sentence, a significant design may use its existing\\narchitecture decision. Trivial changes need no separate comparison document.\\n\\nThese are human review standards. They introduce no separate KISS artifact,\\nmandatory score, receipt, automated simplicity gate or additional approval.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"29e9b6296f39215c4b2ad36659c0674f0b20650682db9aa1187fc97871cfdb06\"}]}]}\r\n",

Reuse unchanged instructions and recover them after compaction.\\n\\n## Private lifecycle test copy\\n\\nWhen the approved task explicitly selects the hosted rehearsal, use the installed\\ncandidate client's `remote rehearse --test-copy` command and the closed v2 request\\nschema in `server/contracts/lifecycle-v2.json`. Do not\\nreplace the retained base with a later head to omit changed files.\\nKeep the head, operation key and exact receipt path in transient working material\\nbefore continuing. Check that every selected requirement (REQ) has the specification (SPEC)\\n   and verification contract (VER) coverage defined in [Complete work scope](WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#complete-work-scope).\\n5. Apply `## work_order` \\u2192 `### Checklist` in\\n   `docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md`.\\n6. Include its draft in the proposed package.\\n8. Run the validation command below.\\n9. Correct findings within the proposed drafts. Rerun validation after edits.\\n   Report unrelated findings separately. Retain findings that need a decision\\n   or an accepted-definition amendment as unresolved dependencies.\\n10. Run the selected-work check below for each proposed work order (WO).\\n    Supply every planned file from Expected change surface with\\n    `--planned-path`. Inspect `scope.preparation`: resolve uncovered or\\n    invalid paths in the draft before requesting approval. A successful\\n    command exit does not establish coverage or a complete impact analysis.\\n    Explain future generated destinations using\\n    [Generated outputs](WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#generated-outputs).\\n11. Present the outcome, scope, artifact IDs and paths, validation results,\\n    unresolved decisions (DEC), and unapplied amendments. Include the\\n    evaluator's reported next action for each selected work order (WO).\\n\\n| Field or section | Content |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| `Objective` | The outcome this work order (WO) will deliver. |\\n| `In scope` / `Out of scope` | The boundaries from [Define the limits of the change](DEFINE_CHANGE.md#define-the-limits-of-the-change) assigned to this work order (WO). |\\n| `Constraints` | The conditions from [Define the limits of the change](DEFINE_CHANGE.md#define-the-limits-of-the-change) that apply to this work. |\\n| `Expected change surface` | Inspected planned paths, the reason for each, and unresolved destinations. |\\n| `[execution_scope].paths` | Exact repository-relative files or component directories ending in `/`. Use forward slashes; no wildcards, absolute paths, or `..`. |\\n| `Authorized decision envelope` | What the implementer may decide and what requires another accountable decision. |\\n| `Required verification` / `Evidence to record` | The checks and retained outputs defined in [Define how the result will be verified](DRAFT_DEFINITIONS.md#define-how-the-result-will-be-verified). |\\n| `Stop and escalate conditions` | The conditions that require pausing this work. |\\n| `Completion report format` | The required report of completed behavior, checks, limitations, and next accountable decision. |\\n| `[assurance]` | `commit_bound_verification`, its `rationale`, and `decided_by`. Apply the classification rules in [Assurance classification](WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#assurance-classification). Record the human who confirmed the classification; an agent may propose it and record that human's decision. |\\n| `[relations]` | `implements` \\u2192 requirements (REQ); `specifications` \\u2192 specifications (SPEC); `verification` \\u2192 verification contracts (VER); `architecture` \\u2192 applicable architectures (ARCH) and required architecture decisions (ADR). |\\n\\nFor PR-based work, include the proposed [review-publication grant](AUTHORITY.md#review-publication-authority)\\nin the decision envelope. Name its repository, source branch, target branch\\nand selected work. Include both the ready-record publication and the later\\ndecision-only push in the expected scope. Present that grant explicitly with\\nimplementation approval; do not infer it from ordinary work authority.\\n\\nIf the assurance classification has not been confirmed, present it as a\\nproposal in the review handoff. Report the missing decision. Do not fill\\n`decided_by` with the draft author's name or an example identity to satisfy\\nvalidation. The human may confirm the classification while reviewing the\\nwork order; record that decision before previewing approval.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\nFor each new work order (WO), run the creation sequence from [Draft any missing definitions](DRAFT_DEFINITIONS.md#draft-any-missing-definitions).\\nInspect the preview before creation; replace `WO-ID` with its `allocated_id`:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl create-artifact REPO --domain DOMAIN --type work_order --dry-run --json\\nharnessctl create-artifact REPO --domain DOMAIN --type work_order --id WO-ID --json\\n```\\n\\nValidate the formal artifacts after completing the drafts and links:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl validate REPO --json\\n```\\n\\nInspect each proposed work order (WO) using its actual ID:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact WO-ID --json\\n```\\n\\nTo assess the proposed file list, repeat `--planned-path` for every file:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact WO-ID --planned-path PATH --planned-path ANOTHER-PATH --json\\n```\\n\\nThis option is available only when the selected released evaluator supports\\nit. If it is unavailable, report that version gap; do not run candidate\\nsource to govern the repository.\\n\\nThe optional planning view evaluates no checkpoint. It reports explicit\\nscope matches, existing automatic admission, uncovered paths and invalid\\ndeclarations. It does not inspect dependencies for the agent, prove that\\nthe supplied list is complete, or turn planned paths into observed changes.\\nDo not combine it with checkpoint or actual-change inputs.\\n\\nValidation does not approve the change. The checkpoint-free `check` reports\\nlifecycle context without evaluating checkpoint gates.\\n\\n**Completion:** Draft work orders (WO) are presented for review with their\\ngoverning artifacts and evaluator results. Every unresolved dependency is\\nidentified. Preparation does not approve or start execution.\\n\\n**Later use:** The authorization process reviews this artifact package,\\nresolves approval blockers, and applies permitted lifecycle transitions.\\nOnly the formal artifacts carry lasting definitions and work authority;\\ntransient working material is not persisted in the repository.\\n\\n## Read next when\\n\\nA proposed package is ready \\u2192 [AUTHORIZE_WORK.md#procedure](AUTHORIZE_WORK.md#procedure).\\n\"}\r\n",

  "aggregated_output": "{\"resources\": [{\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\hag-context-correction34-20261011\\\\codex-291\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"892ec2fedefc272f6bc2580268395e487f392cf5d92a3ea81fac015761bc87a8\", \"bytes\": 8641, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"links-from-work-orders-wo\", \"title\": \"Links from work orders (WO)\", \"anchor\": \"links-from-work-orders-wo\", \"start_line\": 3, \"end_line\": 28, \"content\": \"## Links from work orders (WO)\\n\\nA work order (WO) selects the definitions and verification contracts (VER) that govern\\nits execution. Links to requirements (REQ) alone are not enough.\\n\\n| Source \\u2192 target | Relation | Meaning and coverage |\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\n| Work order (WO) \\u2192 Requirement (REQ) | `implements` | Names every requirement (REQ) in the authorized work scope. |\\n| Work order (WO) \\u2192 Specification (SPEC) | `specifications` | Names the specifications (SPEC) governing those requirements (REQ). |\\n| Work order (WO) \\u2192 Architecture (ARCH) or Architecture decision (ADR) | `architecture` | Names every applicable architecture (ARCH) and every required architecture decision (ADR). |\\n| Work order (WO) \\u2192 Verification contract (VER) | `verification` | Names the verification contracts (VER) for the work. |\\n\\nFor example, a work order (WO) can declare these links in its metadata. The IDs\\nbelow are examples, not records created by this document.\\n\\n```toml\\n[relations]\\nimplements = [\\\"REQ-EXAMPLE-001\\\"]\\nspecifications = [\\\"SPEC-EXAMPLE-001\\\"]\\nverification = [\\\"VER-EXAMPLE-001\\\"]\\n```\\n\\nThe referenced requirement (REQ) must also link back to a capability (CAP) and intent (INT).\\nAdd architecture (ARCH) links when architecture (ARCH) applies; do not invent them just to\\nfill a field.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"e5892787048f79f437b0395f9e1269152ce3d1d1b6fb28994f42849bd12a4f54\"}, {\"heading\": \"complete-work-scope\", \"title\": \"Complete work scope\", \"anchor\": \"complete-work-scope\", \"start_line\": 47, \"end_line\": 65, \"content\": \"## Complete work scope\\n\\nEvery requirement (REQ) selected by a work order (WO)\\nMUST link back to active capabilities (CAP) and intents (INT). It MUST also\\nhave selected active specifications (SPEC) and verification contracts (VER).\\nReuse existing artifacts where their scope applies.\\n\\nA work order should cover one complete bounded outcome, including its\\nforeseeable tests, documentation and retained evidence. Use exact file paths\\nby default. Use a narrow existing component directory when the affected\\nfiles belong to that component. A matching directory does not authorize\\nunrelated behavior.\\n\\nPrepare this scope through\\n[Draft work orders](DRAFT_WORK_ORDERS.md#prepare-work-orders-wo-linking-the-definitions-scope-planned-work-and-verification-requirements).\\nDo not split predictable supporting changes into extra work orders merely\\nbecause they use different file types. A genuine expansion after approval\\nstill needs the applicable human decision; preserve the approved history.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"021ca3cdecffebe415ce9df445c0c48e24a0acde7609d25220c0fb7d470e054e\"}, {\"heading\": \"assurance-classification\", \"title\": \"Assurance classification\", \"anchor\": \"assurance-classification\", \"start_line\": 86, \"end_line\": 116, \"content\": \"## Assurance classification\\n\\nEach work order (WO) in `approved` or\\n`in_progress` MUST set `assurance.commit_bound_verification` to `required`\\nor `not_required`.\\n\\nUse `required` when later decisions depend on the correctness of changes to\\ncode, required checks, CI configuration, harness policy, artifact definitions,\\nor their links. These are examples of \\u201cchanged trusted state\\u201d: information or\\nbehavior that others will rely on when accepting, releasing, or operating the\\nresult.\\n\\nFor example, a work order (WO) changes the code that validates artifact links.\\nA later release decision relies on that validation being correct. The work\\norder (WO) therefore needs verification tied to its exact candidate commit.\\n\\nUse `not_required` only when the work solely records or transports a\\nverification, release, supersession, publication, or deployment decision\\nthat an authorized human has already made. It does not make a new decision\\nor change the definitions, implementation, or evidence behind that decision.\\n\\nFor example, a work order (WO) commits an already authorized release decision\\nin a release record (RLS), with no change to the released code, scope, or\\nsupporting evidence. The work records the decision; it does not reassess the\\nrelease.\\n\\nA work order (WO) that combines both kinds of work MUST be split or classified\\n`required`. `not_required` removes the obligation to prepare a new\\nverification record (VREC) for that work; it does not remove required checks\\nor the links to verification contracts (VER).\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"6ad947ba93cfc84640c82a0b165448ce2c15f04beed36f65a3dc031e4287aab3\"}, {\"heading\": \"generated-outputs\", \"title\": \"Generated outputs\", \"anchor\": \"generated-outputs\", \"start_line\": 66, \"end_line\": 85, \"content\": \"## Generated outputs\\n\\nExisting scope rules admit the selected work order's own file, records that\\ndirectly verify or release that work order, and those records' declared\\nevaluator-evidence paths. This does not admit those records' parent directories.\\nThe selected work order's own packet directory is also already admitted by\\nthe existing scope rules; the planning report identifies that separate rule.\\n\\nList other planned evidence, review and log destinations explicitly in the\\nwork order's scope unless an existing rule covers them. A neighboring file\\nor a record linked only to another work order is not automatically admitted.\\nThe conditional rule for recording risks during execution remains unchanged;\\nit is not a blanket admission of future files during preparation.\\n\\nIf a future record's ID is not allocated, mark its destination as unresolved\\nand explain the relationship rule expected to cover it. Do not create a\\nrecord or invent an ID to complete the plan. Once the evaluator prepares\\nthe record, assess its actual returned record and evidence paths. An\\nunresolved destination is not an already covered file.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"21cb2760e5cf61158c5d19cca2af8dbe727ecf3df32247987cc1636059bde3e9\"}]}, {\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\hag-context-correction34-20261011\\\\codex-291\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"71de2cc92a470e2da25d525e3ad002b77faedb6ef0e69e2fa476a2fa4cb78ff5\", \"bytes\": 11691, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"work_order\", \"title\": \"work_order\", \"anchor\": \"work_order\", \"start_line\": 136, \"end_line\": 146, \"content\": \"## work_order\\n\\n### Checklist\\n\\n- `[execution_scope].paths` is exact: files or component-prefix directories, nothing wider.\\n- `[assurance]` is classified and its rationale names what later decisions depend on.\\n- In scope and out of scope are both stated; the decision envelope says what the implementer may and may not decide.\\n- Stop conditions and the completion report format are stated.\\n- Is every planned change needed for the agreed outcome? Include removal or adjustment of obsolete behavior, tests and instructions within the approved scope.\\n- Inspect supporting paths before approval and assess the supplied plan through [Draft work orders](harness/DRAFT_WORK_ORDERS.md#prepare-work-orders-wo-linking-the-definitions-scope-planned-work-and-verification-requirements). Keep reasons in Expected change surface; do not add a separate planning artifact.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"e8d3be9bfae6d0679a08544ac587fa73e1a26e026d23373c29e1927e0803e7b8\"}]}]}\r\n",

\"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\hag-context-correction34-20261011\\\\codex-291\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\reference\\\\server\\\\contracts\\\\lifecycle-v2.md\", \"sha256\": \"9f1c02ef540c00fa739beb6521295ba9b068f3ab66ff0b0b196cb95810dcd601\", \"bytes\": 5989, \"text\": \"# Private lifecycle rehearsal wire contract\\n\\nThe v2 endpoint accepts only `lifecycle-v2.json`. Every request and result selects\\ntest data. Git remains authoritative for real work. Existing v1 routes and the\\nseven read-only MCP tools keep their contract; they cannot dispatch v2 actions.\\nIn an explicitly configured test project their results use\\n`se-harness-graph-read/v2`, with a required test-copy label. Ordinary Phase 2\\nprojects retain their v1 read result shapes. Revision byte hashing is unchanged;\\ntest revisions add explicit test-copy provenance, without rewriting v1 fixtures.\\n\\n`inspect` accepts check, preflight and validate. `preview` runs a mutation in a\\ndiscarded projection and returns its input digest and complete proposed file\\neffects. `apply` requires that digest, reruns the released checks, and commits\\nthe complete result once. A preview never changes graph state. Actor strings\\nare synthetic test inputs, not authenticated human consent.\\n\\nThe digest binds project/context versions, all selected revision IDs, retained\\nsnapshot, exact command/file inputs, principal and released evaluator identity.\\nMode and operation key are excluded from the preview binding, but included in\\nthe accepted request digest used for principal-scoped retry lookup.\\n\\n## Permitted file effects\\n\\n| Action | Permitted effects in the disposable projection |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| check / preflight / validate | No file writes |\\n| transition | Only selected newly authored artifacts and evaluator sidecars declared by their records |\\n| decide | Selected new decision and its explicitly linked rehearsal risk |\\n| raise-risk | New risk and optional paired decision at released domain paths |\\n| handoff | Declared bounded file inputs within the selected work order's scope; released handoff packet and evaluator evidence |\\n| capture-verification | New VREC and its released evaluator sidecar |\\n| prepare-release | New RLS and its released evaluator sidecar |\\n\\nHandoff first uses the released procedure's fixed `evidence` preparation command,\\nthen `check --checkpoint handoff --from-git`. It exposes no arbitrary evidence\\ncommand. File inputs cannot alter formal records, harness selection/instructions,\\nGit configuration, hooks, or executables used by the service. The service never\\nruns source tests. The local qualification runner supplies observed test evidence.\\n\\nThe adapter enumerates every regular file before and after the operation. It\\nrejects deletions, links, unexpected paths, missing sidecars, imported-record\\nchanges and evaluator failure before opening an acceptance transaction.\\n\\n## Snapshots and Git\\n\\nEach accepted operation retains an immutable complete snapshot: exact file bytes,\\nself-contained Git history and its source/test-candidate identities. Content\\ndigests bind the snapshot to the resulting baseline. Context heads, artifact\\nrevisions, snapshot and receipt share one database transaction. Temporary Git\\nrepositories are discarded after the result is accepted or refused.\\n\\nCapture first commits the exact input projection as test candidate P. P excludes\\nthe new VREC. The output retains the input hosted baseline B, source fixture S,\\nP and evaluator identity. Actual implementation candidate C is recorded separately\\nby qualification. Subsequent commits never alter the candidate stored in a VREC.\\n\\nExport selects an immutable baseline, checks its complete snapshot and Git bundle,\\nand returns exact bounded bytes. The installed client writes only to a new explicit\\ndestination and leaves an incomplete marker until every file hash is checked.\\nNo export writes to or synchronizes an authoritative repository.\\n\\n## Bounds and failure categories\\n\\nKeep 4 MiB requests, 2 MiB responses, 1 MiB individual file inputs, two concurrent\\nprojections, 120-second evaluator calls and 10,000 retained artifact revisions.\\nA pilot snapshot/export that exceeds the response bound is refused atomically.\\nRetained complete snapshots have a separate explicit project count bound of 128.\\nThis is a small private pilot, not an unbounded document store.\\n\\nBoundary/malformed requests, stale inputs, evaluator refusals, invalid output and\\nunknown transport outcomes remain distinct. Read the operation receipt after a\\nlost reply. A changed request under the same accepted key is a conflict. The\\nservice does not automatically rerun a mutation at a newer version.\\n\\n## Bounded Cypher reads\\n\\nThe existing `cypher` MCP/HTTP read selects one exact view. Its request uses the\\nread schema, not the lifecycle command schema. Read the public labels and\\nproperties in [the physical representation](../../docs/notes/hosted-artifact-graph.md#physical-representation)\\nbefore selecting a query. `Artifact` and `Revision` are distinct public labels.\\n\\nThe admitted form has one `MATCH` or `OPTIONAL MATCH` path, labelled nodes,\\noptional parameterized property comparisons, `RETURN`, and a numeric `LIMIT`.\\n\\nRelationship paths are supported. Use `-[edge:TYPE]->` or `<-[edge:TYPE]-` between\\nlabelled nodes, with a public relationship type from the physical representation.\\nEach node and relationship needs a distinct variable name. Anonymous relationship\\nsyntax such as `-[:TYPE]->` is refused; a refusal of that form does not mean\\nrelationship traversal is unsupported. Return-column aliases (`AS alias`) are\\noptional.\\n\\nFor example, with `parameters` containing a selected artifact ID under `artifact`:\\n\\n```cypher\\nMATCH (r:Revision) WHERE r.artifact_id = $artifact RETURN r.artifact_id AS id, r.status AS status LIMIT 10\\n```\\n\\nUse the response's completeness fields with the requested row/byte/depth budget.\\nThis example supplies no project filter: the service binds the selected project\\nand view. Unlabelled nodes, `WITH`, aggregation and arbitrary database syntax are\\nnot part of this small public read form. A rejected query has not completed a read.\\nKeep the exact refusal; consult the documented form before constructing another\\nrequest. Do not weaken query admission or bypass it through a direct database call.\\n\"}]}\r\n",

The delegation MUST name the right, its scope, the granting human,\\nand the receiving human. It MUST be recorded before the delegated decision.\\nThe receiving human MUST decide under their own identity.\\n\\nAn instruction for an agent to apply a recorded human decision delegates the\\nexecution of that command. It does not delegate the decision itself. The\\nagent MUST NOT supply a new answer, broaden the targets, or claim the human\\nmade a decision that was not given.\\n\\nRepository policy MAY require different people for conflicting decisions on\\nthe same candidate. When it does, the same human MUST NOT hold both decisions\\nfor that candidate. A human MUST NOT approve their own architecture decision\\nassessment unless they explicitly hold approval authority for that artifact\\nand the separation rules permit it. Drafting an assessment grants no such\\nright.\\n\\nWhen the accountable human or required authority is absent or ambiguous, stop\\nthe affected decision. State the exact right and artifact needing an owner.\\nDo not substitute an available human or agent merely to fill the field.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"f07389fbbe529ad544d8b7d7f18894bfa45f0ec69996c93ed8372416b55ddf91\"}]}, {\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/RESULTS.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\hag-context-correction34-20261011\\\\codex-291\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\RESULTS.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"090e0172a78ebedfe4cdbe98e74c171e50215766a4ebbd671844a89af3f72e6e\", \"bytes\": 5242, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"report-a-lifecycle-result\", \"title\": \"Report a lifecycle result\", \"anchor\": \"report-a-lifecycle-result\", \"start_line\": 13, \"end_line\": 46, \"content\": \"### Report a lifecycle result\\n\\nAfter a lifecycle stage completes or reaches a stop condition, obtain the\\nselected evaluator's schema-2 result. The result controls the reported scope,\\neffects, blockers, final state, required decision, alternatives, and next step.\\nThe human or agent MUST NOT recompute those fields.\\n\\nFor a human-readable report, lead with the outcome or required decision. The\\nwording and headings may vary, and empty fields may be omitted. The report\\nMUST preserve:\\n\\n1. The actual artifact IDs and whether the selected operation completed or\\n   was blocked.\\n2. The observed effects, separately from expected effects that did not occur.\\n3. Every exact blocker and every material non-effect. In particular, do not\\n   imply approval, a transition, verification, release, a Git action,\\n   publication, deployment, or operation that did not occur.\\n4. The final lifecycle state and the accountable human or agent. When a\\n   decision is required, name the exact decision and authority needed.\\n5. Exactly one current typed procedure step from the evaluator.\\n6. The command's argument values and boundaries, or the operative meaning of\\n   the suggested response.\\n\\nOnly complete alternatives declared by the workflow may be shown. Present them\\nseparately from the primary next step. Do not invent an effect, authority,\\nblocker, decision, or alternative. Do not add unrelated repository findings\\nto the selected result. Do not replace the returned next step with an\\nopen-ended question about what to do next.\\n\\nAutomation MUST read the structured JSON result. New results declare\\n`digest_format = \\\"machine-fields-v1\\\"`. This digest binds machine fields such\\nas candidate identity, scope, state, gates, and command arguments. Explanatory\\nwording is excluded. Older retained results keep their original digest format.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"d12f5fc7e6190762622666754fde9b70e658249ceb41f2fdbf48e5e0edbd0f8f\"}]}]}\r\n",

Read the exact artifacts and matching evidence; linked records do not change automatically.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"12caf4e1a109fcba5c36d2c720480cdc6b95c019128c651aa8da620fadd2ed68\"}, {\"heading\": \"complete-a-selected-definition\", \"title\": \"Complete a selected definition\", \"anchor\": \"complete-a-selected-definition\", \"start_line\": 13, \"end_line\": 50, \"content\": \"### Complete a selected definition\\n\\n**Inputs:** An approved definition, its completion evidence, and the exact\\ndecision from the human authorized for that definition.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifact:** The selected definition becomes `implemented` with a\\n  lifecycle-history entry if the permitted transition succeeds.\\n- **Transient working material:** The preview, apply result, and readback.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Read the selected definition and its current state.\\n2. Confirm that its content and evidence match the human's completion decision.\\n3. If completion is already recorded, report that state; do not replay it.\\n4. Preview the exact transition below.\\n5. Inspect every target, actor, gate result, and reported effect.\\n6. Apply the same transition only when it matches the decision and passes.\\n7. Read the artifact and new history entry. Preserve any refusal.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl transition REPO --set DEFINITION-ID=implemented --decision DEFINITION-ID=HUMAN --json\\nharnessctl transition REPO --set DEFINITION-ID=implemented --decision DEFINITION-ID=HUMAN --apply --json\\n```\\n\\nThe selected release does not accept definition IDs in `check`. The transition\\npreview supplies the legality and gate result. Do not change a definition's\\nstate by hand to make it selectable.\\n\\n**Completion:** Completion is recorded on that definition, or the exact\\nrefusal is known. Linked work orders keep their states.\\n\\n**Later use:** Select a related work order by its actual ID and use its current\\n`check` result. A completed definition does not select or start all linked work.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"376e69a74eb756254c8e9cd9feba1818526fb640934cc16cc8ed7e5eda7bb426\"}]}]}\r\n",

Before using its execution grant, read [AUTHORITY.md#authority-from-work-approval](AUTHORITY.md#authority-from-work-approval). For a scope finding, read [RESULTS.md#if-a-procedure-is-blocked](RESULTS.md#if-a-procedure-is-blocked).\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"5581ca4e192b2a3847952cdb19582916ed96242a14941b1e5a8a610be996e1dd\"}, {\"heading\": \"start-the-selected-work\", \"title\": \"Start the selected work\", \"anchor\": \"start-the-selected-work\", \"start_line\": 70, \"end_line\": 104, \"content\": \"### Start the selected work\\n\\n**Inputs:** The approved work order (WO), actual executor identity, and\\ncurrent execution context.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** The selected work order (WO) becomes `in_progress`\\n  with a lifecycle-history entry when start succeeds.\\n- **Transient working material:** Start-check and transition results.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. If the work order (WO) is already `in_progress`, inspect the recorded start\\n   and resume unapplied work. Do not replay the start transition.\\n2. Otherwise, run start preflight under the existing approval.\\n3. Preview the transition to `in_progress` using the actual executor identity.\\n4. Apply the same transition only when preflight and the preview pass.\\n5. Inspect the resulting state.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl preflight REPO --work-order WO-ID --phase start --json\\nharnessctl transition REPO --set WO-ID=in_progress --decision WO-ID=ACTOR --json\\nharnessctl transition REPO --set WO-ID=in_progress --decision WO-ID=ACTOR --apply --json\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact WO-ID --json\\n```\\n\\n**Completion:** The selected work order (WO) is `in_progress`, or its start\\nis blocked with an explicit reason. Existing approval covers a permitted\\nstart; no duplicate human start decision is required.\\n\\n**Later use:** [Implement the approved scope](EXECUTE_WORK.md#implement-the-approved-scope) performs the authorized implementation.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"2275126fa8b418eccbaacb1972d0140709337470ba8d190b6566fd16854328d1\"}]}, {\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/AUTHORITY.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\hag-context-correction34-20261011\\\\codex-291\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\AUTHORITY.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"da7202bf8d1beee631e9b4b5ba01c04b440fbf76d200ccbccbb8781a59f88431\", \"bytes\": 16163, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"authority-from-work-approval\", \"title\": \"Authority from work approval\", \"anchor\": \"authority-from-work-approval\", \"start_line\": 134, \"end_line\": 163, \"content\": \"## Authority from work approval\\n\\nWork-order approval authorizes execution of its approved scope: start,\\nimplementation, local edits and commits, required checks, evidence capture,\\ncompletion recording, and required verification-record preparation. A Human\\nand an Agent MUST use the same local approval, scope, and evidence checks.\\nContinue these operations without asking for the same permission again while\\ntheir scope and conditions still match. Record execution under the actual\\nexecutor's identity.\\n\\nApproval leaves the work order `approved` until its start transition is\\napplied. Selecting and scheduling work remain explicit. New approvals need\\nno separate execution delegation table or second start approval. A preliminary\\nmerge and live CI are not local execution requirements; CI still applies at\\nintegration and publication.\\n\\nThe grant does not include changed scope, acceptance of the result, release,\\nmerge, publication, or other external action. Reuse an existing explicit\\nauthorization for such an action only when its exact target and conditions\\nstill match.\\n\\nHistorical approvals keep their original meaning. Earlier explicit execution\\ngrants remain usable under the same scope checks. An older approval without\\nsuch a grant needs an authorized amendment for the remaining execution.\\nCurrent metadata or an actor label MUST NOT manufacture that historical grant.\\nIf the installed release cannot record the required authorization, stop the\\nremaining execution and report the missing historical grant and the lack of\\na supported amendment operation. Do not insert invented grant fields or\\nrewrite the old approval.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"a0ce00fccb8c1c8833455c14fe3ec75eaf01c597f0a1f46a24f7962ab1958f8c\"}]}]}\r\n",

  "aggregated_output": "{\"resources\": [{\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/EXECUTE_WORK.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\hag-context-correction34-20261011\\\\codex-291\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\EXECUTE_WORK.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"f094e7bc796ba1002c3fb2848adaccce6c4887e3d92503911bcafa4504a644fe\", \"bytes\": 11979, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"implement-the-approved-scope\", \"title\": \"Implement the approved scope\", \"anchor\": \"implement-the-approved-scope\", \"start_line\": 105, \"end_line\": 154, \"content\": \"### Implement the approved scope\\n\\n**Inputs:** The work order (WO) in `in_progress`, approved definitions,\\npermitted paths, and baseline from [Establish the execution context](EXECUTE_WORK.md#establish-the-execution-context).\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Repository files:** The code, tests, documentation, or configuration\\n  changes authorized by the work order (WO).\\n- **Formal artifacts:** No lifecycle transition in this step. Review the diff against the accepted definitions. Apply\\n   [Review of implemented changes](../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#review-of-implemented-changes).\\n7. Resolve in-scope defects. Stop affected work when a finding requires changed\\n   requirements, paths, or authority.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\nRepeat `--changed-path PATH` for the complete set, including planned new files:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact WO-ID --checkpoint scope --changed-path PATH --changes-complete --json\\n```\\n\\nThis declaration is checked evidence, not independent proof of completeness.\\nWhen the selected procedure requires a `pre-action` check, use its returned\\ncommand with the complete change-set inputs. For Git-derived actual changes:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact WO-ID --checkpoint pre-action --from-git BASE --json\\n```\\n\\nUse the repository's editing, build, and test tools for implementation.\\n`harnessctl` does not implement the change.\\n\\n**Completion:** The approved behavior is implemented within scope, or the\\nremaining work and blocker are explicit. No completion state is inferred yet.\\n\\n**Later use:** [Retain the implementation evidence](EXECUTE_WORK.md#retain-the-implementation-evidence) checks the result and retains its evidence.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"fccc0b61295d1a2fb0b7f7a3323063932bed26eafce5d7f592a432d9493ec944\"}, {\"heading\": \"retain-the-implementation-evidence\", \"title\": \"Retain the implementation evidence\", \"anchor\": \"retain-the-implementation-evidence\", \"start_line\": 155, \"end_line\": 210, \"content\": \"### Retain the implementation evidence\\n\\n**Inputs:** The implemented changes, verification contracts (VER), required\\nrepository checks, and work-order evidence locations.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Retained evidence files:** Actual check results, review findings, their\\n  resolution, and Git-derived handoff evidence at authorized evidence paths.\\n- **Formal artifacts:** Evidence references may be added where the work order\\n  (WO) requires them. No lifecycle state changes here.\\n- **Transient working material:** A summary of remaining evidence gaps.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Run every required check using its specified inputs and environment.\\n2. Retain the command arguments, working directory, runtime identity, exit\\n   status, output, and relevant file paths or digests.\\n3. Preserve failed results alongside later corrections and successful reruns.\\n4. Retain the material diff-review findings and their resolution.\\n5. Confirm that all required evidence files exist at the locations named by\\n   the work order (WO) or verification contract (VER).\\n6. Run review preflight.\\n7. Run the Git-derived handoff check with the trusted `BASE` from [Establish the execution context](EXECUTE_WORK.md#establish-the-execution-context).\\n8. Inspect its written evidence and reported findings. Correct in-scope gaps\\n   and rerun affected checks.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl preflight REPO --work-order WO-ID --phase review --json\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact WO-ID --checkpoint handoff --from-git BASE --json\\n```\\n\\nFor ordinary files listed in the work order\\u2019s `evidence_paths`, confirm that\\neach file exists inside the repository and contains the required evidence.\\nThese files do not need a machine header. Use the supported evidence command\\nfor generated packets; do not edit their evaluator-owned binding fields.\\n\\nThe Git-derived handoff command writes retained evidence. Confirm its output\\npaths are covered by the approved preparation scope. If the evaluator calls\\nfor creating or rebinding the handoff evidence packet, use:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl evidence REPO --artifact WO-ID --checkpoint handoff --json\\n```\\n\\nThis command also writes a file. It does not run tests or make an unsupported\\nclaim true. Rerun the required handoff check after correcting the evidence gap.\\n\\n**Completion:** Required implementation checks pass and the actual evidence\\nis retained, or the exact missing or failed checks remain visible.\\n\\n**Later use:** [Record implementation completion](EXECUTE_WORK.md#record-implementation-completion) requires passing handoff results. Verification later\\nassesses these retained files; they are not disposable planning notes.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"4cccfe03ac5fe219da997051bb91053576f18e67e834f0036f93e9856e8f12a2\"}, {\"heading\": \"record-implementation-completion\", \"title\": \"Record implementation completion\", \"anchor\": \"record-implementation-completion\", \"start_line\": 211, \"end_line\": 257, \"content\": \"### Record implementation completion\\n\\n**Inputs:** Completed work, passing handoff checks, retained evidence, and\\nthe unchanged approved execution scope.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** The selected work order (WO) becomes `implemented`\\n  with the actual executor recorded in its lifecycle history.\\n- **Transient working material:** The completion report and current next step.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Confirm that the work and required evidence are complete.\\n2. Preview the completion transition using the executor's own identity.\\n3. Apply the same transition when the preview passes.\\n4. Inspect the resulting work order (WO).\\n5. Report the completed behavior, checks, limitations, and evaluator's next\\n   action. Preserve failures if completion was refused.\\n\\nUse the passing handoff result from the preceding step. A passing completion\\npreview does not replace the handoff check. If the implementation, governing\\nartifacts, or required evidence changed after handoff, rerun the affected\\nchecks before applying completion. If `harnessctl` refuses the retained\\nhandoff evidence, follow its reported corrective step.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl transition REPO --set WO-ID=implemented --decision WO-ID=ACTOR --json\\nharnessctl transition REPO --set WO-ID=implemented --decision WO-ID=ACTOR --apply --json\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact WO-ID --json\\n```\\n\\n**Completion:** The work order (WO) is `implemented`, or its completion is\\nblocked. Completion does not verify, release, or deliver the result.\\n\\n**Later use:** Work requiring commit-bound verification proceeds to\\n[Verify the outcome](VERIFY_OUTCOME.md#establish-the-verification-scope).\\nAfter preparation, PR-based work first follows [Publish the review package](PULL_REQUEST.md#publish-the-review-package).\\nThen use the [verification request](VERIFY_OUTCOME.md#obtain-the-humans-verification-decision)\\nwhen the ready record is eligible and its PR is confirmed. Local-only work\\nuses that verification request without a PR. The completion report introduces no\\nadditional human approval. An implemented work order (WO) classified `not_required`\\nneeds no new verification record (VREC); follow its actual next action and\\nany separately authorized delivery instruction.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"e9c897ed3281727176649c1a128308da088e0f04282645d2c43a4c7a9a795649\"}]}, {\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\hag-context-correction34-20261011\\\\codex-291\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"8dbc5fb4bb80fc3c2fbf1ec34a2419e8b5856972485226af46ae324fbd9aca5c\", \"bytes\": 11817, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"before-this-action\", \"title\": \"Before this action\", \"anchor\": \"before-this-action\", \"start_line\": 7, \"end_line\": 10, \"content\": \"## Before this action\\n\\nBefore writing, read [Links for decisions and risks](RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md#links-for-decisions-and-risks), [Blocking decisions](RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md#blocking-decisions) and [Raised risks](RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md#raised-risks). Apply [../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#risk](../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#risk) or [../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#decision](../ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#decision) for the selected record.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"e8a14639d6c2512ed5f9bfea0f7bfd9d4a2e428642e8fc8a02d600f792ab846f\"}, {\"heading\": \"record-risks-risk-affecting-the-change\", \"title\": \"Record risks (RISK) affecting the change\", \"anchor\": \"record-risks-risk-affecting-the-change\", \"start_line\": 13, \"end_line\": 65, \"content\": \"### Record risks (RISK) affecting the change\\n\\n**Inputs:** The outcome, scope, selected definitions, verification coverage,\\nand existing risks (RISK) found in [Identify the existing artifacts that apply to the change](DEFINE_CHANGE.md#identify-the-existing-artifacts-that-apply-to-the-change).\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** New risks (RISK) in `raised` for threats not already\\n  covered. A paired decision (DEC) in `open` for each risk created with\\n  `--with-decision`. None created where existing records cover the threats.\\n- **Transient working material:** The selection of reused risks (RISK),\\n  review notes, generated IDs and paths, and links awaiting new work order\\n  (WO) IDs. If no risks are identified, retain that result with the reviewed\\n  scope. Retain this material under the same conditions as [Describe the intended outcome](DEFINE_CHANGE.md#describe-the-intended-outcome).\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Identify what could go wrong within the selected change scope.\\n2. Check whether an existing risk (RISK) already records each threat and its\\n   follow-up. Reference that record instead of creating a duplicate.\\n3. For each new risk (RISK), describe the threat and why it matters.\\n4. Identify its follow-up owner.\\n5. Specify the owner's next action.\\n6. Identify the formal artifacts threatened by it.\\n7. Determine whether an unresolved decision must block those artifacts.\\n8. Preview the risk (RISK) with the command below. Inspect the proposed\\n   content, affected IDs, and destination paths.\\n9. Run the same command with the same arguments, removing only `--dry-run`.\\n10. Read every written file reported by the command. Retain its ID and path\\n    for the review handoff.\\n\\n**Harness command:**\\n\\nReplace the quoted text and `OWNER` with the risk description and identified\\nowner. Repeat `--threatens ARTIFACT-ID` for each threatened artifact. Omit that\\noption if no affected formal artifact exists yet:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl raise-risk REPO --domain DOMAIN --title \\\"Risk title\\\" --description \\\"What could go wrong and why it matters\\\" --action \\\"Next follow-up action\\\" --owner OWNER --threatens ARTIFACT-ID --dry-run --json\\n```\\n\\nAdd `--with-decision` only if action 7 identifies a decision (DEC) that must\\nblock the named artifacts. Use the same option in both preview and creation.\\nA risk (RISK) alone does not block work.\\n\\n**Completion:** Identified risks (RISK) have formal records with an owner and\\nnext action. If none were identified, retain `None identified` with the\\nreviewed scope as transient working material.\\n\\n**Later use:** Review any paired decision (DEC) in [Record unresolved decisions (DEC)](RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md#record-unresolved-decisions-dec). [Prepare work orders (WO) linking the definitions, scope, planned work, and verification requirements](DRAFT_WORK_ORDERS.md#prepare-work-orders-wo-linking-the-definitions-scope-planned-work-and-verification-requirements) uses the\\nrisks (RISK) to define work and stop conditions and adds links that depend on\\nnew work order (WO) IDs.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"8431175790f8bf07019c19f9cb51d6ee5186b8bc66fccfbb2665ab99fc5028e9\"}, {\"heading\": \"raised-risks\", \"title\": \"Raised risks\", \"anchor\": \"raised-risks\", \"start_line\": 176, \"end_line\": 187, \"content\": \"## Raised risks\\n\\nA risk (RISK) in `raised` may have no paired decision\\n(DEC). Recording that risk alone does not block work. Use\\n`raise-risk --with-decision` when creating a risk that needs a paired blocking\\ndecision.\\n\\nA raised risk MUST NOT have more than one paired decision in `open` or\\n`deferred`. When that decision exists, it names the risk in `concerns`, and\\nits `blocks` set MUST equal the risk's `threatens` set. Disposing the paired\\ndecision applies its recorded effect to the risk in the same operation.\\nThe blocked artifacts change state only through their own transitions.\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"dcbef84857f6b71fbfa2099de79f6caa4d82e8977b13465eccb762ffc3a9ea1e\"}]}]}\r\n",
