{
  "id": "item_90",
  "type": "command_execution",
  "command": "\"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\.cache\\\\codex-runtimes\\\\codex-primary-runtime\\\\dependencies\\\\native\\\\powershell\\\\pwsh.exe\" -Command '& \"C:/Users/mathi/AppData/Local/Python/pythoncore-3.14-64/python.exe\" -I \"C:/Users/mathi/Documents/Codex/2026-09-20/verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se/work/hag-context-correction34-20261011/codex-291/native/inputs/native_call.py\" instructions --section \"docs/engineering/harness/RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md#links-for-decisions-and-risks\" --section \"docs/engineering/harness/RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md#blocking-decisions\" --section \"docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#risk\" --section \"docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md#decision\" --section \"docs/engineering/harness/AUTHORIZE_WORK.md#resolve-approval-blockers\"'",
  "aggregated_output": "{\"resources\": [{\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\hag-context-correction34-20261011\\\\codex-291\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\RISKS_AND_DECISIONS.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"8dbc5fb4bb80fc3c2fbf1ec34a2419e8b5856972485226af46ae324fbd9aca5c\", \"bytes\": 11817, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"links-for-decisions-and-risks\", \"title\": \"Links for decisions and risks\", \"anchor\": \"links-for-decisions-and-risks\", \"start_line\": 132, \"end_line\": 149, \"content\": \"## Links for decisions and risks\\n\\n| Source \\u2192 target | Relation | Meaning and coverage |\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\n| Decision (DEC) \\u2192 any artifact type | `concerns` | Names every artifact the question is about. |\\n| Decision (DEC) \\u2192 Requirement (REQ), Specification (SPEC), Verification contract (VER), Architecture (ARCH), Architecture decision (ADR), or Work order (WO) | `blocks` | Names artifacts whose transitions the decision (DEC) blocks. Each must also appear in `concerns`. |\\n| Decision (DEC) \\u2192 Requirement (REQ), Specification (SPEC), Verification contract (VER), Architecture (ARCH), Architecture decision (ADR), or Work order (WO) | `produces` | A decision (DEC) in `decided` names artifacts its answer created or amended, when applicable. |\\n| Risk (RISK) \\u2192 any artifact type | `threatens` | Names the artifacts the risk (RISK) could damage. |\\n| Risk (RISK) \\u2192 Work order (WO) | `mitigated_by` | Names the work orders (WO) reducing a risk (RISK) in `mitigating` or `mitigated`. The decision operation writes this link. |\\n| Risk (RISK) \\u2192 Architecture decision (ADR) or Decision (DEC) | `avoided_by` | Names the single architecture decision (ADR) or decision (DEC) that removes a risk (RISK) in `avoided`. The decision operation writes this link. |\\n\\nA decision (DEC) records a question that needs an answer or a proposed deviation.\\nAn architecture decision (ADR) records a settled design choice. They serve different purposes.\\n\\nA risk (RISK) does not block work by itself. When a blocking decision (DEC)\\nis requested, that decision (DEC) concerns the risk (RISK). The `blocks` set\\nof the decision (DEC) matches the `threatens` set of the risk (RISK).\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"5009680651d50038248f4c60c5fceaf6065393bf7b3b2f370c54560ba83dd63a\"}, {\"heading\": \"blocking-decisions\", \"title\": \"Blocking decisions\", \"anchor\": \"blocking-decisions\", \"start_line\": 150, \"end_line\": 175, \"content\": \"## Blocking decisions\\n\\nA decision (DEC) in `open` blocks every transition\\nof the artifacts in its `blocks` relation. A decision (DEC) in `deferred`\\nblocks transitions outside its recorded permitted scope.\\n\\nFor example, a decision (DEC) names work order (WO) `WO-EXAMPLE-001` in both\\n`concerns` and `blocks`. It is deferred with the scope\\n`WO-EXAMPLE-001:approved-in_progress`. This deferral\\nallows the work order (WO) to move from `approved` to `in_progress` if all\\nother checks pass. It still blocks moving that work order (WO) from\\n`in_progress` to `implemented`. The deferral also records when the decision\\n(DEC) must be revisited. Deferral does not itself start the work.\\n\\nAn accepted deviation is a decision (DEC) with `kind = \\\"deviation\\\"`,\\n`status = \\\"decided\\\"`, and `disposition.option = \\\"accept\\\"`.\\nIt records permission to depart from one identified specification (SPEC)\\nrule; \\u201caccepted\\u201d is not a separate lifecycle state for the decision (DEC).\\n\\nThat deviation remains applicable to the affected specification (SPEC),\\nwork orders (WO), and their verification records (VREC) and release records\\n(RLS) until a later decision (DEC) against the same rule reaches\\n`status = \\\"decided\\\"` with `disposition.option` set to `amend` or\\n`supersede`. The disposition is written through `harnessctl decide`, not\\nby editing the metadata by hand.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"ed29cb785085f0704b9ab61f95ab42f2ee01579c0d191cb6587ce6c97684cdc0\"}]}, {\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\hag-context-correction34-20261011\\\\codex-291\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"71de2cc92a470e2da25d525e3ad002b77faedb6ef0e69e2fa476a2fa4cb78ff5\", \"bytes\": 11691, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"risk\", \"title\": \"risk\", \"anchor\": \"risk\", \"start_line\": 188, \"end_line\": 198, \"content\": \"## risk\\n\\n### Checklist\\n\\n- Record a description, an owner and a next action.\\n- Use `harnessctl raise-risk --description TEXT --action TEXT --owner ROLE` with a domain and title.\\n- Stage, category, threatened artifacts and scoring are optional. If scoring is useful, supply likelihood and impact together (1\\u20135); the command computes their product.\\n- Request `--with-decision` only when the owner needs a decision that blocks named artifacts. A risk by itself does not block work.\\n- Keep earlier scores, decisions and dispositions as recorded; no migration is required.\\n\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"8815c9ff38ca34594404ab95cb0545053e209804030f3d635a50641d33559de9\"}, {\"heading\": \"decision\", \"title\": \"decision\", \"anchor\": \"decision\", \"start_line\": 171, \"end_line\": 187, \"content\": \"## decision\\n\\nA pending question becomes a `decision` (`DEC-`) when it blocks a transition\\nof another artifact, concerns more than one artifact, or must survive the\\napproval of the artifact that raised it. Below that threshold the actor asks\\nand the answer stays in the transition's `reason`.\\n\\n### Checklist\\n\\n- `kind` is `question` (an ambiguity met while authoring or planning) or `deviation` (an implementation cannot meet one rule of one specification). *(mechanical)*\\n- One `question`, `raised_by`, at least two `[[options]]` with `id` and `label`, and a `recommendation` naming one option. *(mechanical)*\\n- A deviation also names `against = \\\"SPEC-xxx#PREFIX-AREA-NNN\\\"`, a rule identifier the specification defines *(mechanical: E-DCM-005)*, and the `observed` fact; its options are drawn from `amend`, `supersede`, `accept`, `stop` and include `stop`. *(mechanical)*\\n- `concerns` names every artifact the question is about; `blocks` names the artifacts that cannot change state while it is `open`, each also in `concerns`. *(mechanical)*\\n- The `[disposition]` table is written by `harnessctl decide`; a hand-written one is `E-DCM-003`. A deferral needs a scope and a revisit trigger; accepting a deviation needs a revisit trigger. *(mechanical)*\\n- `decided` and `withdrawn` decisions are never deleted or rewritten.\\n- The definition templates carry no `Open decisions` section: a definition's pending decisions are the `DEC-` artifacts that name it in `blocks`, and the approval gate reads them from the graph. A legacy section, where one remains, reads `None` or lists `DEC-` identifiers; prose there is `E-DCM-004`.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"b3fdcc8578aac9039cf6513b13851f7a35a63027fde6dd1afeb34593a23e083b\"}]}, {\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/AUTHORIZE_WORK.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\hag-context-correction34-20261011\\\\codex-291\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\AUTHORIZE_WORK.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"991b526d6280554dcca6901c1790e5519b8894e08635a1f10618aa84a29aaf28\", \"bytes\": 15212, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"resolve-approval-blockers\", \"title\": \"Resolve approval blockers\", \"anchor\": \"resolve-approval-blockers\", \"start_line\": 84, \"end_line\": 159, \"content\": \"### Resolve approval blockers\\n\\n**Inputs:** The findings from [Assess the proposed artifact package](AUTHORIZE_WORK.md#assess-the-proposed-artifact-package) and the affected draft artifacts or\\npending decisions (DEC).\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** Corrected drafts within the proposed scope. Where an\\n  actual human decision is supplied, the selected decision (DEC) receives its\\n  disposition. A paired risk (RISK) may change through that same operation.\\n- **Transient working material:** The resolution of each finding and any\\n  remaining dependency requiring an amendment or another human decision.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Correct incomplete or inconsistent draft content within the requested scope.\\n2. Return an accepted-definition change to the amendment procedure in\\n   \\u201cDefine the change.\\u201d Do not edit accepted authority to clear a check.\\n3. For a blocking decision (DEC), inspect its current question and options.\\n4. Obtain the accountable human's exact answer if it has not already been given.\\n5. Preview that disposition with the command below.\\n6. Apply the same command with `--apply` only if its inputs match the actual\\n   decision and the preview passes.\\n7. Read back the decision (DEC) and any paired risk (RISK).\\n8. Rerun the checks affected by the corrections. Preserve unresolved blockers.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact DEC-ID --json\\nharnessctl decide REPO --artifact DEC-ID --option OPTION-ID --decision ACTOR --reason \\\"Exact decision reason\\\" --json\\n```\\n\\nUse a declared option ID. Add `--revisit \\\"Trigger\\\"` for acceptance of a\\ndeviation. A risk-mitigation option also requires `--mitigated-by WO-ID` for\\neach selected mitigating work order (WO). For a risk-avoidance option, use\\n`--avoided-by ARTIFACT-ID` when naming a separate architecture decision (ADR)\\nor decision (DEC). Review the returned operation before applying it.\\n\\nACTOR is the actual human who made the decision. If that human acts under an\\nexisting owner label, first resolve their authority under\\n[Decision rights](AUTHORITY.md#decision-rights), then add\\n`--authority-owner OWNER` to both preview and apply. For example, a human\\nnamed `mmzen` acting under `engineering-owner` uses\\n`--decision mmzen --authority-owner engineering-owner`. Do not put the owner\\nlabel in place of the human. Neither string authenticates the decision.\\nOWNER must be non-blank printable text of at most 128 characters and match\\nan eligible owner exactly. An unrelated label refuses without writing.\\n\\nFor an explicitly authorized deferral, use this preview instead:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl decide REPO --artifact DEC-ID --defer --scope ARTIFACT-ID:FROM-TO --revisit \\\"Trigger\\\" --decision ACTOR --reason \\\"Exact decision reason\\\" --json\\n```\\n\\nRepeat `--scope` for each permitted transition. For an explicitly authorized\\nwithdrawal, replace the option or deferral arguments with `--withdraw`.\\nApply a passing preview by repeating the exact command with `--apply`.\\nThen inspect the decision (DEC) again and rerun validation:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact DEC-ID --json\\nharnessctl validate REPO --json\\n```\\n\\nIf proposing a departure from a `SHOULD` rule, record the rule ID, reason,\\nimpact, accountable human or agent, and compensating evidence. Present these\\nwith the affected review finding. Recording the departure does not authorize\\nan action or waive a required check.\\n\\n**Completion:** Each blocker is resolved or assigned an explicit outstanding\\ndecision. A deferral clears only its recorded transition scope.\\n\\n**Later use:** [Obtain the human's decision](AUTHORIZE_WORK.md#obtain-the-humans-decision) receives the corrected package. Unresolved blockers\\nremain visible and prevent the affected approval.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"ead7ade46e1090c644d789a5ca1155415aa2497561938b885e8316cd13aeb920\"}]}]}\r\n",

The private\\nservice and candidate remote client are implemented under WO-HAG-001. Development\\nqualification is retained in VREC-HAG-004. Use [the operating procedure](../../server/README.md) to build and test\\nthe exact combination. Git remains authoritative. This is not a public service.\\n\\nDEC-HAG-001 is decided. The bounded revision in DEC-HAG-002 selects public\\nevaluator 0.22.1 for this sandbox; candidate client 0.22.2 is separate.\\n\\nPhase 3 adds an explicit private test-copy lifecycle pilot under WO-HAG-008 and\\nSPEC-HAG-007. Git remains authoritative. The pilot uses separately versioned\\n[closed operations](../../server/contracts/lifecycle-v2.md), exact multi-file\\nsnapshots and ordinary disposable Git history. Its eight required VER-HAG-006\\nscenarios passed, and mmzen verified\\n[VREC-HAG-005](../engineering/hosted-artifact-graph/verification-records/VREC-HAG-005.md).\\nPR #542 integrated that result. The separate native Codex/Claude qualification is\\n[in progress under WO-HAG-009](../engineering/hosted-artifact-graph/evidence/WO-HAG-009/report.md).\\nAuthentication and database ACL implementation remain deferred. The existing\\nprivate access controls and RISK-HAG-001 remain in place.\\n\\n## Project and source identities\\n\\nThe explicit operator initialization command allocates a UUIDv4 `project_id`\\nonce and stores it on Project with `command_version = 0` and `schema_revision = 1`.\\nAn operator may supply a fixed UUID for a reproducible disposable test. Repeating\\ninitialization confirms the same identity; it cannot silently replace a store.\\nThe readable name `hosted-artifact-poc` is a display name, outside revision hashes.\\nClients obtain the UUID from initialization output or authenticated status.\\nRequests never allocate projects and never take a principal identity on trust.\\n\\nThe reference source is `https://github.com/mmzen/se_harness`, Git SHA-1 commit\\n`82f5a0ed7438a73da8f03aee23ad02a9b8cc09e1`. The source manifest lists every formal\\nartifact path, ID, blob OID, byte length and raw SHA-256. Generate it from Git\\nblobs using the released discovery list, not Explorer output or a worktree read.\\nOn Windows, `git archive` needs `-c core.autocrlf=false`: archive defaults can\\nconvert LF to CRLF even when the blob is LF. Compare each exported artifact with\\n`git cat-file` bytes. Preserve original bytes, including CRLF when present in Git.\\n\\nThe operator mounts the pinned source/evidence snapshot read-only. Import requests\\nidentify this configured source; they cannot make the server fetch URLs or read\\narbitrary host paths. Check every manifest entry against its mounted bytes, then\\nuse the released parser for the canonical artifact set. Missing, duplicate,\\nextra or conflicting entries prevent complete import. Supporting code/evidence\\nbelongs to the immutable historical resolver, outside the 64 MiB artifact limit.\\n\\n## Revision and baseline bytes\\n\\n`server/contracts/remote-v1.json` names the exact fields. A StoredRevision contains\\n`revision_id`, `envelope` and `document_base64`. The envelope binds the full raw\\ndocument SHA-256; the store verifies it against decoded bytes. Imported provenance\\ncontains the original repository/object format/commit and Git blob OID. Draft\\nprovenance records the authenticated principal, operation key and server-assigned\\ncreation time once. An accepted retry returns the retained bytes and time.\\n\\nCanonical JSON uses UTF-8 without BOM, sorted object keys, compact separators,\\nliteral Unicode, no Unicode normalization and no floats. Reject duplicate object\\nkeys and non-finite numbers before decoding into a map. Semantic sets are sorted\\nand deduplicated before encoding: relation targets, artifact selection keys and\\nresolved relation triples. Preserve meaningful sequence order. Raw document\\nbytes receive no line-ending or Unicode conversion for the new revision scheme.\\n\\nThe revision hash input is `se-harness-artifact-revision/v1`, LF, then canonical\\nenvelope bytes. `revision_id` is `sha256:` plus the lowercase hex digest. The\\nbaseline hash input uses `se-harness-artifact-baseline/v1`, LF and the canonical\\nmanifest; its identifier is that scheme plus `:sha256:` and the hex digest.\\nNeither hash payload includes its own derived ID or a future verification record.\\nThe baseline manifest binds sorted selection, resolved revision-to-revision\\ntriples, provenance and the exact evaluator identity. A missing relation target\\nprevents a complete baseline. Saved incomplete drafts remain distinct from\\ncomplete frozen selections and from approved definitions.\\n\\nThe fixture file `canonical-v1.json` supplies exact JSON strings and hash-input\\nbytes for three connected draft artifacts, LF/CRLF, composed/decomposed Unicode,\\na body edit, sequence order and a baseline. These are synthetic byte examples,\\nnot claimed receipts. Its all-zero parent baseline is an explicit fixture marker.\\nFuture serializer tests must consume these fixed expectations; do not regenerate\\nexpected hashes from serializer output.\\n\\n## Command-specific fields\\n\\nEvery mutation carries the project ID, operation key, expected project version,\\nexact evaluator archive/payload identity, and candidate client version/wheel hash.\\nThe server checks compatibility against the qualified tuple before mutation.\\nThe authenticated principal comes from credentials; claimed component identity\\ndoes not grant authority. Reject unknown fields and contradictory selectors.\\n\\n| Operation | Required selection and content | Accepted effect |\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\n| `import` | Complete configured source manifest; no baseline/context selector | Original immutable revisions and imported baseline, deterministic report, receipt, one project-version increment |\\n| `draft-open` | Base baseline ID and selected work-order ID | New UUID context at version 0; unchanged base; receipt and project-version increment |\\n| `create-artifact` | Context ID/version, domain, supported type; ID or explicit null for allocation | New draft revision and proposed selection; context and project versions increment once |\\n| `revise-artifact` | Context ID/version, artifact ID, expected selected revision, complete base64 document | New draft revision and derived relations; replace only that context selection; increment both versions |\\n| `freeze` | Context ID/version | New immutable baseline from the resolved complete view; project version increments; context stays open with its original base and version |\\n\\nAn empty project has no baseline to select. Import therefore has no view selector.\\nOperation lookup is `GET /v1/projects/{project}/operations/{key}` and is scoped to\\nthe authenticated principal. It requires neither a baseline nor a current version.\\nReadiness also has no view selector. These are the applicable-field interpretations\\nof HAG-API-001/002, not changes to the named protocol schemes.\\n\\nThe draft view is its base plus explicit proposals. New IDs are reserved across\\nall retained project artifacts, not just the selected baseline. The command adapter\\nuses the released authoring template and allocation behavior in a disposable\\nprojection. The isolated public 0.22.1 evaluator supplies standalone draft\\nadmission. Protected lifecycle/provenance/evidence fields remain protected.\\n\\nFreeze does not rebase, close, clear or otherwise change its context. Editing that\\ncontext later creates another proposed revision. Opening a fresh context from\\nthe frozen baseline explicitly selects a new base. Repeating an already accepted\\noperation key returns its original receipt even if live versions have advanced.\\nA different request under the same principal/project/key returns conflict.\\n\\n## Atomic acceptance and reads\\n\\nBind evaluation to project version N and the exact context/revision selection.\\nIn a short explicit database transaction, conditionally change the same Project\\nguard from N to N+1 and recheck context/revision guards. Commit the new content,\\nderived edges, selection changes and accepted receipt in that transaction. A\\ncompeting guard update or constraint conflict refuses; a process mutex is not\\nthe transaction boundary. Do not retry against newer input without caller action.\\n\\nImported content and repeated source identity cannot disagree. Reimporting the\\nsame complete source may return the already present immutable baseline; it must\\nnot duplicate revisions or change the stable import report. A new operation key\\nstill has its own guarded command/receipt; retrying the original key has no new\\neffect. A refusal creates no accepted receipt.\\n\\nDomain reads select either an immutable baseline or an explicit context/version.\\nExact revision, work context, comparison, impact, verification lineage and check\\nall return selection identity, provenance, evaluator identity and completeness.\\nComparison explicitly names both views. Check is read-only and checkpoint-free;\\nit reports released findings and cannot apply a lifecycle transition. Operation\\nlookup returns the recorded receipt, not a recomputed result at the latest view.\\nUnsupported live-view forms are refused until their semantics are qualified.\\n\\nDomain and MCP reads share handlers. Context completeness requires all selected\\ngoverning artifacts and declared paths; truncated results cannot establish a\\ngoverning claim. The pinned reference fixture has 12 governing IDs and 11 paths\\nfor WO-RLS-038; VREC dependencies remain separately classified.\\n\\n## Validation at each stage\\n\\n| Stage | Required assessment | Meaning of success |\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\n| Decode | Strict UTF-8, unique JSON keys, integer-only request numbers, closed wire shape, contained source paths and configured source identity | A request can be evaluated; no authority or mutation follows from decoding |\\n| Import | Complete Git manifest, raw byte/provenance equality, released parsing and relation validation, all referenced targets resolved | A faithful historical baseline; imported lifecycle claims acquire no new decision event |\\n| Draft creation/revision | Released standalone draft classification, server rights, protected-field comparison and exact input selection | A saved draft may retain the evaluator's narrow permitted incompleteness; malformed content or supplied invalid relations refuse |\\n| Freeze | Complete selection, resolvable declared edges, canonical manifest and version guards | An immutable baseline of that selection; draft members remain drafts |\\n| Context/read/check | Explicit view, exact released context/findings, original-path historical resolver and honest resource limits | A bounded observation; `complete` does not mean approved or gate-passing |\\n| Approval/verification/release | Unsupported in this sandbox | No remote command can confer a human decision or produce a verified/released record |\\n\\nThe draft stage uses the selected public 0.22.1 evaluator. Its archive and payload\\nare fixed by SPEC-HAG-003. Earlier Phase 1 reports retain their original 0.22.0\\nobservations and unresolved-dependency status as historical evidence.\\n\\n## Read request and response details\\n\\n`server/contracts/read-v1.json` defines the seven POST request variants and their\\nresponse shapes. HTTP path operation/project and body values must agree. MCP\\nuses the same normalized request and authenticated handler. A context selector\\nrequires its exact version. If that version has changed, refuse with 409; no\\nimplicit latest view or historical context reconstruction is promised. Freeze a\\nselection when later reads need an immutable identity. A compare request names\\ntwo views in the same project.\\n\\n| Read | Selection and returned data |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| `revision` | Artifact ID and revision ID must match the selected view. Return the complete StoredRevision, including raw bytes; a known revision outside that view is an unknown selected identity |\\n| `work-context` | Selected work order, governing bindings, exact declared paths, dependencies and relevant decisions in separate fields; embed the unchanged checkpoint-free evaluator result |\\n| `compare` | Added/removed/changed artifact bindings plus added/removed resolved relation triples; a missing side of a binding is null |\\n| `impact` | The root and reverse reachability through known declared relations at the selected view, within depth; exclude the root from the returned artifact list |\\n| `lineage` | The root and connected declared verification/evidence relations, with endpoint revisions; this reports recorded links and claims, not new assurance |\\n| `check` | Only a WO, VREC, RLS or DEC accepted by the selected released checkpoint-free `check`; return its JSON unchanged with the selected binding |\\n| `cypher` | Columns and rows from the admitted query, bound to the selected view; column names and row widths agree and graph values expose only the documented public properties |\\n\\nSort domain bindings by artifact ID, paths lexically, and edges by\\n`(source.artifact_id, kind, target.artifact_id)`. Preserve evaluator output and\\nCypher row order. A read's `provenance` names the unique Git sources of its selected\\ninputs; synthetic draft-only examples may have none. Draft provenance is retained\\nin each revision envelope. Resolve every returned revision through the view.\\nFor comparison, resolve each side independently. These equality and resolution\\nchecks require the service; JSON Schema checks only their shapes.\\n\\n`complete=true` means that this response contains the whole requested answer at\\nthe stated view and no unresolved references. It can still contain draft hints,\\nopen decisions, failed gates or a missing historical binding in the unchanged\\nevaluator result. When missing bindings prevent the requested assessment, report\\n`complete=false` with `binding_unavailable` and identify the exact missing input\\nin evaluator output. Do not convert `not_assessable` into a pass.\\n\\nBudgets apply to the aggregate graph rows across all returned collections, not\\n500 rows per nested array. Paths and unresolved-reference entries also consume\\nthat allowance. The byte budget includes the entire serialized response and\\nembedded evaluator output; never truncate that JSON. Traversal stops must be\\nvisible even if the last returned node has no displayed outgoing edge. A bounded\\npartial response uses `complete=false`, the specific limit and concrete\\ninstructions to repeat at the same view with a narrower selection. That strategy\\ndoes not turn a partial work context into a governing claim. If the operation\\nhas no meaningful narrower selection, repeat with a larger budget within the\\nfixed limits; if the minimum honest response cannot fit, refuse with 429.\\nUnresolved graph targets require a new complete view, not silent continuation at\\nan altered context version. No pagination cursor or server-side read session is\\nintroduced in this initial contract.\\n\\nThe baseline GET retrieves one canonical manifest resource, not a row query:\\n`{schema: \\\"se-harness-artifact-baseline/v1\\\", baseline_id, manifest}`. Validate the\\nmanifest with `BaselineManifest`, recompute its identity, and return the full\\nselection and resolved relations. The 2 MiB response limit still applies; reject\\nan import/freeze whose complete baseline response cannot fit before committing.\\nDo not clip the manifest to the graph-query row budget or label a fragment as B.\\nOperation GET returns exactly the stored accepted `remote-result/v1` object for\\nthe authenticated principal/project/key. Status GET reports project UUID, schema\\nrevision, readiness, actual evaluator and component identities, and the supported\\nprotocols. Missing built/qualified identities keep readiness false. Neither GET\\nrequires a context selector; operation lookup never guesses an acceptance.\\n\\n## Accepted receipts, refusals and retry order\\n\\n`server/contracts/result-v1.json` defines immutable accepted receipts and stable\\nremote refusal codes. Every successful mutation returns HTTP 200 and one UUIDv4\\n`receipt_id`. Store that entire result with the operation. Bind `request_digest`\\nto SHA-256 of `se-harness-remote-command/v1`, one LF, and canonical JSON of the\\ncomplete validated command. Canonicalize manifest entries as their declared set\\nbefore hashing; retain original document bytes and all expected versions. Reject\\nduplicate manifest entries before normalization. Credentials, connection metadata\\nand transport timestamps are outside the command and digest.\\n\\nAn accepted result's project `after` equals `before + 1`. For context open,\\ncontext `before` is null and `after` is zero. Create/revise increments the context\\nonce; freeze reports equal context versions. Import has a null context version\\nrecord. The returned view names the imported/frozen baseline or resulting context;\\naffected revision IDs are sorted unique IDs created by this operation, so an\\nidentical-source reimport may report none. Receipt IDs are correlation identities,\\nnot substitutes for revision or baseline hashes.\\n`affected_artifacts` supplies the corresponding artifact/revision bindings, so\\ncreation with automatic ID allocation returns the allocated artifact ID directly.\\nIts revision set must equal `affected_revision_ids`; a refusal returns both empty.\\n\\nApply checks in this order:\\n\\n1. Authenticate and enforce project/operation access, then perform bounded strict\\n   decoding and shape checks. Reject unknown fields such as caller-supplied actor.\\n2. For a valid command, compute its request digest and inspect the accepted key.\\n   Equal digest returns the original result immediately, even after versions or\\n   the configured tuple change. Different digest returns key-reuse conflict.\\n   Current project access remains required; never evaluate a retry as a new write.\\n3. For a new key, check the supported tuple, known selections, then project,\\n   context and selected-revision guards in that order. Refuse the first mismatch.\\n4. Check source/protected input and invoke the released evaluator against the\\n   bound selection. Invalid draft/import, incomplete freeze and unavailable\\n   mandatory bindings have distinct 422 codes. Resource refusal is 429.\\n5. Recheck guards and selection in the write transaction, write all effects and\\n   receipt, then commit. On a concurrent equal-key conflict, read the winner's\\n   committed receipt. Never update a stale request's expectations automatically.\\n\\nMalformed input uses 400, unauthenticated 401, forbidden 403, unknown accessible\\nidentity 404, stale/key/source/tuple conflict 409, invalid content 422 and resource\\nrefusal 429. The schema enumerates the `HAG_REMOTE_*` codes. These codes wrap the\\nremote operation; existing evaluator codes and JSON remain unchanged. Refusals\\nhave no receipt and no affected revisions. Populate correlation/view/versions\\nonly when known and authorized; otherwise use null. When versions are returned\\non refusal, before equals after. Read refusals use null command correlation and\\nversions. Denial must not leak another project's identities or findings.\\n\\nThe schemas describe the selected evaluator profile as well as wire shapes.\\nTheir pinned evaluator constants are compatibility checks: a well-formed but\\ndifferent version/archive/payload is 409, not malformed JSON. Keep those checks\\nseparate from primitive shape decoding and accepted-key recovery. Strictly\\ndecode base64 and require its canonical encoding before digest calculation;\\ninvalid base64 is malformed input, while invalid decoded TOML is invalid draft\\ncontent. A successful shape check alone never supplies an admission decision.\\n\\nA lost response, evaluator process crash or ambiguous database commit is not an\\naccepted or refused receipt. The client reports transport uncertainty and uses\\noperation lookup or an identical retry. A 404 lookup alone cannot prove that a\\nconcurrent transaction rolled back. A known precommit failure leaves no effects;\\nan unknown commit must be reconciled against the authoritative operation store.\\n\\n## Scenario and schema qualification\\n\\n`tests/hosted_artifact_graph/fixtures/scenarios-v1.json` maps all twelve\\nVER-HAG-001 cases to explicit positive/failure outcomes and storage support. Every\\nhosted execution entry is `unperformed`. Its wire examples contain synthetic\\nidentities and demonstrate shape only; their apparent receipt values are not\\nobserved acceptances. The original fixed canonical vectors remain unchanged.\\n\\nFor independent shape qualification, install `jsonschema==4.26.0` in a disposable\\nenvironment and run its Python against:\\n\\n```text\\npython -I -B tests/hosted_artifact_graph/validate_wire_contracts.py\\npython -m unittest tests.test_hosted_artifact_graph\\n```\\n\\nThe first command registers the three local schemas without network resolution,\\nvalidates fixed vectors and the complete source manifest, and exercises accepted\\nand rejected shapes. It does not introduce a core runtime dependency. The second\\ncommand checks fixed bytes and digests through the existing test entry point.\\nNeither command executes service admission, transactions, Cypher or recovery.\\n\\n## Physical representation\\n\\nProject stores identity, schema revision and the integer command guard. Artifact\\nstores project-scoped identity. Revision stores its canonical `envelope_json`,\\n`document_base64`, artifact ID, raw document digest and derived type/status.\\nBaseline stores `manifest_json`; its SELECTS edges are derived from that manifest.\\nDraftContext stores base baseline, selected work order, version and proposals.\\nOperation stores project/principal/key, semantic request digest and immutable\\n`result_json`. JSON text properties retain exact machine structures without\\nexpanding scalar fields into graph nodes.\\n\\nHAS_REVISION links Artifact to Revision. SELECTS links Baseline to Revision.\\nBASED_ON links DraftContext to Baseline. PROPOSES links DraftContext to Revision\\nwith the selected artifact ID. DECLARES links Revision to the target Artifact,\\nwith `kind` and `target_artifact_id`; resolve the target revision through the view.\\nCross-project edges, duplicate selections, and edges inconsistent with canonical\\ncontent fail import/export checks. Unresolved authoring placeholders remain\\nexplicit findings and cannot become invented valid target nodes.\\n\\nThe public Cypher surface uses the selected project's Artifact and Revision\\nnodes, its selected Baseline (or context/base), and the corresponding storage\\nedges above. Project exposes only project ID, schema revision and the observed\\ncommand version. Artifact exposes project/artifact IDs. Revision exposes its IDs,\\ntype, status, document digest, envelope JSON and document base64. Baseline exposes\\nits IDs and manifest JSON. DraftContext exposes its IDs, selected work order,\\nbase baseline and context version. DECLARES exposes kind and target artifact ID;\\nPROPOSES exposes the selected artifact ID. Other edge properties are not public.\\n\\nOperation nodes and their result JSON are private to command handling and the\\nprincipal-scoped operation lookup. They are not available through Cypher. A\\nquery cannot use internal labels/properties, an unselected revision, another\\nbaseline/context, or caller-authored project filters to widen this surface. The\\nservice must apply that projection before query execution and use the same\\nread-only transaction snapshot for selection and results. This is application\\nadmission; it does not resolve RISK-HAG-001 or prove database privileges.\\n\\n`graph-v1.cypher` supplies six composite/single uniqueness keys, key/content\\nexistence constraints and explicit lookup indexes. Memgraph requires separate\\nindexes for uniqueness constraints ([official constraint documentation](https://memgraph.com/docs/fundamentals/constraints)).\\nSchema creation must be an explicit operator step on an empty store; later\\nstartup verifies it and refuses mismatch. Explicit initialization, stored revision\\nmismatch and missing-index refusal have now been tested for the exact candidate\\nin the [qualification report](../engineering/hosted-artifact-graph/evidence/WO-HAG-001/phase2-20261005/protocol04-assessment.md).\\n\\n## Deferred boundary and historical qualification\\n\\nCypher remains part of the sandbox: parse a narrow read grammar, constrain the\\nselected view, apply row/byte/depth/time limits and roll back the read transaction.\\nDatabase-enforced read-only access remains RISK-HAG-001; no authoritative-pilot or\\npublic-service claim is made. The current contract does not authorize a parser\\nbypass, a replacement lifecycle policy or suppression of malformed input.\\n\\nThe candidate now includes its dependency lock, image/Compose files, admission\\nadapter, transaction implementation, remote client and plugin guidance. The\\npackaged-client walkthrough, live concurrency and refusal checks, independent\\nevaluator comparison and restart/restore have passed for candidate\\n`7290af984337e122b193981a187e58c29de41a16`. The linked report preserves earlier\\nfailures and exact component identities.\\n\\nThe [later Claude qualification](../engineering/hosted-artifact-graph/evidence/WO-HAG-001/claude-20261006/report.md)\\nuses candidate `5fa50787dba1fdd010f625335d844416dd3bf002`. Authentication works;\\nthe corrected MCP schemas allow all seven native tools. The guided CLI sequence,\\nHTTP/MCP response comparison and repeated live boundary suite pass. Claude still\\nmisreported a large partial response as complete. A smaller follow-up was correctly\\nreported; it does not erase that failure.\\n\\nThe [Codex continuation](../engineering/hosted-artifact-graph/evidence/WO-HAG-001/codex-20261006/report.md)\\non that same candidate completes 18 installed-client operations and seven native\\nMCP reads, with exact HTTP parity and correct partial-result reporting. It retains\\nthe original wheel-access and MCP approval-policy failures. The successful runs\\nuse the normal host profile and approval reviewer; no persistent permissions were\\nweakened. Exact candidate guidance was read explicitly, so automatic plugin loading\\nand desktop remain unobserved. Earlier restart/restore and evaluator results above\\nremain historical candidate04 evidence. WO-HAG-001 remains in_progress, and PR #535\\nremains draft.\\n\\n\\n## Current Phase 2 qualification\\n\\nThe [current assessment](../engineering/hosted-artifact-graph/evidence/WO-HAG-001/final-20261006/report.md)\\nrecords all twelve required scenarios for the final candidate, its exact component\\ntuple, real native CLI observations and restart/restore. It preserves the earlier\\nfailures above. Large saved MCP responses expose their completeness metadata to\\nbounded file reads. Parser failures preserve their errors without returning an\\nunusable catalog that exceeds the CLI response bound.\\n\\nThe assessment distinguishes tested behavior from human verification. Read the\\nlinked work orders and verification record for current lifecycle state. Codex\\ncandidate guidance was read explicitly; automatic loading and desktop were not\\ntested. Database-side read-only enforcement remains RISK-HAG-001. Do not\\nreclassify a finding because it is labelled `structure`, `governance`, `policy`,\\nor `maintenance`.\\n\\nReport the exact failed rule or predicate, the unchanged affected lifecycle\\nstate, and any effects that already occurred. Preserve the observed evidence.\\nUse the evaluator's current result to report one corrective step or one\\naccountable escalation.\\n\\nFor a failed gate, use the corrective form that `harnessctl check` returns for\\nthe first failing predicate. Do not substitute an unchanged replay of the\\nfailed command. Resolve the missing input, scope, evidence, or decision before\\nretrying the affected action. Remediation that changes scope, accepts risk,\\nor exercises a reserved decision right requires the corresponding explicit\\ndecision.\\n\\nWhen a correction requires implementation, inspect the proposed work order\\nwith `harnessctl check REPO --artifact WO-ID --json`. Reuse it only if its\\napproved scope covers the correction and its current state permits execution.\\nStart approved work through the start procedure; resume work already in\\nprogress. If no eligible work order covers the correction, return to Define\\nthe change and Authorize the work to prepare and approve a new work order.\\nPreserve completed and rejected records. The selected release provides no\\ntransition from `implemented` back to `in_progress`; do not edit a state or\\nreplay an earlier start to reopen it. A correction that changes an accepted\\ndefinition must also follow the linked-revision boundary.\\n\\nAfter an interrupted write or uncertain external action, inspect the actual\\nresult before retrying. Continue only work that has not already occurred.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"08dd44f4f71d3b7ade9b5908371f3b1e9320d63fa9859b6fe2fd3bc5ceaf2bda\"}]}, {\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\hag-context-correction34-20261011\\\\codex-291\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"71de2cc92a470e2da25d525e3ad002b77faedb6ef0e69e2fa476a2fa4cb78ff5\", \"bytes\": 11691, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"review-of-implemented-changes\", \"title\": \"Review of implemented changes\", \"anchor\": \"review-of-implemented-changes\", \"start_line\": 147, \"end_line\": 156, \"content\": \"## Review of implemented changes\\n\\n- Does the result satisfy the necessary contract, and did implementation reveal unnecessary specified behavior?   "aggregated_output": "{\"resources\": [{\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/VERIFY_OUTCOME.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\hag-context-correction34-20261011\\\\codex-291\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\VERIFY_OUTCOME.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"84686ea50e0e220aadc024145b88e05d83a0eab01be361ab50e12716a8cf950a\", \"bytes\": 18538, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"before-this-action\", \"title\": \"Before this action\", \"anchor\": \"before-this-action\", \"start_line\": 7, \"end_line\": 10, \"content\": \"## Before this action\\n\\nFor preparation, read [WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#verification-coverage](WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#verification-coverage). For a decision, read [AUTHORITY.md#decision-rights](AUTHORITY.md#decision-rights) and [AUTHORITY.md#delegation-and-separation](AUTHORITY.md#delegation-and-separation). For supersession only, also read [WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#successor-coverage](WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#successor-coverage). Read the exact candidate and retained evidence required by the selected contract.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"509b10e8e12887c623b12e5997e2baf7bcb193b87a24b63fe19795676bddc8a7\"}, {\"heading\": \"assess-the-verification-evidence\", \"title\": \"Assess the verification evidence\", \"anchor\": \"assess-the-verification-evidence\", \"start_line\": 70, \"end_line\": 107, \"content\": \"### Assess the verification evidence\\n\\n**Inputs:** The selected candidate, accepted definitions, verification\\ncontracts (VER), and retained implementation evidence.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Retained evidence files:** A requirement-by-requirement assessment with\\n  actual check results and unresolved gaps at the specified evidence locations.\\n- **Formal artifacts:** No verification decision or lifecycle transition.\\n- **Transient working material:** Review notes not required as retained evidence.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Compare the candidate's observed behavior with each acceptance criterion.\\n2. Map every required check to its actual evidence file and pass condition.\\n3. Confirm that the evidence applies to the selected candidate and environment.\\n4. Run missing checks using the verification contract's (VER) commands or\\n   manual procedure. Retain their actual results.\\n5. Record each criterion as passed, failed, or not assessed, with its reason.\\n6. Retain material findings and their resolution with the verification evidence.\\n7. For a defect requiring implementation changes, identify a work order that\\n   covers the correction and is eligible for execution. Follow the recovery\\n   rules under \\u201cIf a procedure is blocked.\\u201d A completed work order does not\\n   become executable again because verification found a defect.\\n8. After the authorized correction, establish the new candidate identity and\\n   reassess the affected criteria against evidence for that candidate.\\n\\n**Harness command:** None for the substantive assessment. Use the check\\ncommands and manual assessments defined in the verification contracts (VER).\\nHarness validation alone does not prove the required behavior.\\n\\n**Completion:** Every required criterion has evidence or a visible gap.\\nFailures and missing checks are not reported as passes.\\n\\n**Later use:** [Prepare the verification record](VERIFY_OUTCOME.md#prepare-the-verification-record) binds the retained evidence to a verification record\\n(VREC). [Obtain the human's verification decision](VERIFY_OUTCOME.md#obtain-the-humans-verification-decision) uses it for the human's assessment.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"78a405625bfb24107f4b8f4f09ad84942d5710c55b27d58f3114da5f40688c3b\"}, {\"heading\": \"prepare-the-verification-record\", \"title\": \"Prepare the verification record\", \"anchor\": \"prepare-the-verification-record\", \"start_line\": 108, \"end_line\": 169, \"content\": \"### Prepare the verification record\\n\\n**Inputs:** The exact candidate, selected work orders (WO), their verification\\ncontracts (VER), retained evidence, and existing preparation authority.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** One new verification record (VREC) in `ready` when\\n  capture is required and succeeds. Related work-order (WO) states do not change.\\n- **Retained files:** The generated evaluator evidence and candidate snapshot\\n  or export required by the capture procedure.\\n- **Transient working material:** The capture result and inspected output paths.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. If a suitable verification record (VREC) already exists, inspect it and\\n   continue to [Obtain the human's verification decision](VERIFY_OUTCOME.md#obtain-the-humans-verification-decision). Do not duplicate an interrupted successful capture.\\n2. Confirm preparation authority under every selected work order's (WO)\\n   approval. Reuse it while the scope and inputs match.\\n3. Select an unused `VREC-ID` after checking the repository's local Git refs.\\n4. Confirm the domain and actual record and evidence destinations. Keep all\\n   generated writes within the authorized preparation scope.\\n5. Establish a clean committed candidate using authorized local Git actions.\\n   Retain its full commit ID. Do not discard unrelated changes to obtain it.\\n6. Run the capture command with each selected work order (WO), every declared\\n   verification contract (VER), and each retained evidence file.\\n7. Read the generated record and evaluator evidence. Confirm the candidate\\n   commit, selected IDs, evidence digests, and `ready` state.\\n8. Retain generated records and evidence in a later authorized governance\\n   commit. Preserve the earlier candidate commit that the record assesses.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl capture-verification REPO --id VREC-ID --work-order WO-ID --verification VER-ID --evidence EVIDENCE-PATH --owner ACTOR --domain DOMAIN --json\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact VREC-ID --json\\n```\\n\\nUse the actual preparation actor for `--owner`. Preparation does not record\\na future verification or release decision. Preserve the generated record and\\nits bound evidence without changing the recorded evidence bytes.\\n\\nRepeat `--work-order`, `--verification`, and `--evidence` for every selected\\ninput. `EVIDENCE-PATH` is a repository-relative file, not a directory or an\\nindex whose links will be followed automatically. Capture writes immediately\\nafter its checks; it has no `--dry-run` or `--apply` option.\\n\\nIf an unchanged rebase leaves an earlier ready record bound to the old\\ncandidate, use [Refresh verification after an unchanged rebase](VERIFY_OUTCOME.md#refresh-verification-after-an-unchanged-rebase).\\nA verified source or changed relevant inputs cannot use that shortcut.\\n\\nIf preserving local edits requires the supported committed-candidate route,\\nuse `--candidate-commit COMMIT` with `--test-command EXECUTABLE ARGUMENTS`.\\nPut `--test-command` last. That route tests the named commit in a temporary\\ncheckout; use its actual results and returned record, not results from the\\nuncommitted edits.\\n\\n**Completion:** A ready verification record (VREC) binds the selected candidate\\nand evidence, or capture reports a specific refusal. Preparation is not verification.\\n\\n**Later use:** [Obtain the human's verification decision](VERIFY_OUTCOME.md#obtain-the-humans-verification-decision) presents the exact record and evidence for the human decision.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"34e77e503346373221eaa0bb46e970ee738ce6a5eebbfdece9ba6e8ee36450a1\"}, {\"heading\": \"record-the-verification-decision\", \"title\": \"Record the verification decision\", \"anchor\": \"record-the-verification-decision\", \"start_line\": 255, \"end_line\": 300, \"content\": \"### Record the verification decision\\n\\n**Inputs:** The exact human decision, ready verification record (VREC), and\\nunchanged candidate and evidence inputs.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** Only the selected verification record (VREC) receives\\n  its permitted state and lifecycle-history entry.\\n- **Retained files:** The updated record is retained through authorized Git\\n  actions. Historical candidate and evidence facts are preserved.\\n- **Transient working material:** The observed decision result and next action.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Recheck that the selected inputs still match the human decision.\\n2. Preview the exact transition.\\n3. Apply the same command when its gates pass and effects match the decision.\\n4. Inspect the verification record (VREC) and resulting workflow context.\\n5. Report its actual state, any blocker, and the evaluator's next action.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl transition REPO --set VREC-ID=TARGET --decision VREC-ID=ACTOR --json\\nharnessctl transition REPO --set VREC-ID=TARGET --decision VREC-ID=ACTOR --apply --json\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact VREC-ID --json\\n```\\n\\nFor supersession, select a successor verification record that is already\\n`verified` or `released` and preserves the old record\\u2019s work-order coverage.\\nUse the transition preview to assess that selection.\\n\\nFor `rejected`, add `--reason \\\"VREC-ID=Rejection reason\\\"` to preview and apply.\\nFor `superseded`, add `--reason \\\"VREC-ID=SUCCESSOR-VREC-ID\\\"` to both. Preserve\\nthe old record; do not rewrite its candidate or evidence to match a new result.\\n\\n**Completion:** The selected verification record (VREC) has the recorded\\ndecision. Referenced work orders (WO) and release records (RLS) remain unchanged.\\n\\n**Later use:** For PR-based work, [Publish the verification decision](PULL_REQUEST.md#publish-the-verification-decision)\\nas the final commit under the existing grant. Eligible verified coverage\\nsupports the selected delivery path.\\nA rejection or supersession follows the evaluator's remediation or selection\\nprocedure; it does not authorize new implementation scope.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"99e090908551d2012bdadac654496a2c14eefe9399b04112fcf067f6386854d7\"}]}]}\r\n",

  "status": "completed"
}

  "aggregated_output": "{\"resources\": [{\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\hag-context-correction34-20261011\\\\codex-291\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"892ec2fedefc272f6bc2580268395e487f392cf5d92a3ea81fac015761bc87a8\", \"bytes\": 8641, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"verification-coverage\", \"title\": \"Verification coverage\", \"anchor\": \"verification-coverage\", \"start_line\": 117, \"end_line\": 123, \"content\": \"## Verification coverage\\n\\nA verification record (VREC) MUST bind one or more\\nwork orders (WO), all their declared verification contracts (VER), retained\\nevidence, and one exact clean candidate commit. Preparing a verification\\nrecord (VREC) does not change its state to `verified`.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"d0359e722c997b266376b6644404fca0db87d8718a79d2f2503aca0669936adf\"}]}, {\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/VERIFY_OUTCOME.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\hag-context-correction34-20261011\\\\codex-291\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\VERIFY_OUTCOME.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"84686ea50e0e220aadc024145b88e05d83a0eab01be361ab50e12716a8cf950a\", \"bytes\": 18538, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"obtain-the-humans-verification-decision\", \"title\": \"Obtain the human's verification decision\", \"anchor\": \"obtain-the-humans-verification-decision\", \"start_line\": 170, \"end_line\": 254, \"content\": \"### Obtain the human's verification decision\\n\\nFor work delivered through a PR, first complete\\n[Publish the review package](PULL_REQUEST.md#publish-the-review-package).\\nDo not request verification before the exact remote review package is confirmed.\\nUse the evaluator's declared review-publication alternative, not its later\\nintegration path. Local-only work does not acquire a PR requirement.\\n\\n**Inputs:** The ready verification record (VREC), candidate commit, evidence\\ndigests, assessment results, and accountable human's verification authority.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** None changed by the discussion or read-only gate check.\\n- **Transient working material:** The human's exact verification, rejection,\\n  or supersession decision and reason where required.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Prepare the concise verification request below for the exact record,\\n   candidate, evidence, and unresolved findings.\\n2. For verification or rejection, evaluate the proposed target with the\\n   command below. Supersession gates are evaluated with the selected successor\\n   in [Record the verification decision](VERIFY_OUTCOME.md#record-the-verification-decision)'s transition preview.\\n3. Obtain the accountable human's decision on that exact verification record\\n   (VREC). Preserve the required independence from implementation.\\n4. Reuse a previous decision only while its record, candidate, evidence digests,\\n   authority, and current gates still match.\\n5. For rejection, retain the reason. For supersession, identify the exact\\n   eligible successor verification record (VREC).\\n\\n**Harness command:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact VREC-ID --checkpoint transition --target TARGET --json\\n```\\n\\nUse `verified` or `rejected` for `TARGET`. The evaluator determines whether\\nthat edge is legal. Supersession needs the successor input accepted by\\n`transition --reason`, which this check command does not accept.\\nA passed check is not the human decision.\\n\\n**Verification request:**\\n\\n- **Verification requested - [outcome]:** Name the useful result being assessed.\\n- **Delivered:** Describe the behavior delivered against the agreed outcome.\\n- **Evidence:** Summarize the requirement results and meaningful checks. Link\\n  the requirement-by-requirement assessment and retained evidence. Test counts\\n  support the explanation; they do not replace it.\\n- **Limits:** State material failures, skipped or unavailable checks, unassessed\\n  criteria, and residual uncertainty. Say that no material gaps are known only\\n  when the evidence supports it.\\n- **Your decision:** Explain that \\\"Verify result\\\" accepts this exact candidate\\n  against the agreed requirements. Merge and release remain separate decisions.\\n- **Review details:** For PR-based work, show the confirmed PR URL prominently.\\n  Identify the exact VREC and full candidate commit. Link its governing work\\n  orders, verification contracts, assessment, and evidence at the remote review\\n  commit so the owner can read them without access to the workstation.\\n  Local-only work uses its available review locations.\\n\\nLead with ordinary language and keep the request proportionate to the work.\\nDetails may be linked, but material gaps and the decision's scope must be\\nvisible in the request. Keep passed, failed, and not-assessed results distinct.\\nAn accepted risk needs its recorded decision reference; otherwise it remains\\nunresolved. Do not silently bundle risk acceptance or waive required checks.\\n\\nOffer \\\"Verify result\\\" and \\\"Request corrections\\\" when verification is eligible.\\nIf verification is blocked, report the blocker and evaluator's next action\\ninstead of offering acceptance.\\nThe human need not type IDs or commands. Bind an unambiguous \\\"I verify\\\" or\\n\\\"Verify result\\\" to the displayed record, candidate, and evidence before applying\\nthe decision. Clarify an ambiguous reply. Reassess changed inputs under action 4;\\nsilence or implementation approval does not supply verification acceptance.\\n\\n\\\"Request corrections\\\" leaves the decision pending; it is not a terminal\\nrejection. Follow [Assess the verification evidence](VERIFY_OUTCOME.md#assess-the-verification-evidence)\\nto identify the correction and eligible execution authority. A completed work\\norder does not become executable again. An explicit rejection or supersession\\nstill follows action 5 and [Record the verification decision](VERIFY_OUTCOME.md#record-the-verification-decision).\\n\\n**Completion:** The exact verification decision is known, or the record remains\\npending. No implementation actor infers acceptance from their own passing tests.\\n\\n**Later use:** [Record the verification decision](VERIFY_OUTCOME.md#record-the-verification-decision) records only the selected decision.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"cdf0222448290088f6b56d69941badd6bd3bf0bf60c19e05ddba06b00033f081\"}]}]}\r\n",

  "aggregated_output": "{\"resources\": [{\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/DRAFT_DEFINITIONS.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\hag-context-correction34-20261011\\\\codex-291\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\DRAFT_DEFINITIONS.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"a2041b84342c2b2e4b5ec0f26e3a70702a894c57d9810855cfe514881e5a0c28\", \"bytes\": 13484, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"prepare-a-release-or-operating-contract\", \"title\": \"Prepare a release or operating contract\", \"anchor\": \"prepare-a-release-or-operating-contract\", \"start_line\": 166, \"end_line\": 220, \"content\": \"### Prepare a release or operating contract\\n\\n**Inputs:** A proposed release or ongoing operating obligation, its scope,\\nexisting work-order or requirement IDs, and any accepted contract that may\\nalready cover it.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** A completed release-contract (REL) or operating-contract\\n  (OPS) draft when needed. An accepted contract is reused only if its meaning\\n  and scope already cover the proposed obligation.\\n- **Transient working material:** Selection notes, new IDs and paths, and\\n  unresolved questions. No release or operating authorization is inferred.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Decide which obligation applies: release scope uses `release_contract`;\\n   continuing assurance uses `operating_contract`. Do not create both by default.\\n2. Read existing contracts selected for reuse. If an accepted contract needs\\n   changed meaning, use the accepted-definition amendment boundary; do not edit\\n   it through this draft-creation procedure.\\n3. For a missing contract, use the supported domain and artifact creation\\n   sequence from \\u201cDefine the change.\\u201d Inspect the dry-run result and use its\\n   returned `allocated_id` in the creation command.\\n4. Complete the generated body and accountable metadata. For a REL, record\\n   release scope, version conditions, rollback, and evidence expectations.\\n   For an OPS, record measurable observability, support, and operating obligations.\\n5. Set `REL.gates` to every existing work-order ID covered by the release\\n   contract, or `OPS.assures` to every existing requirement ID for which it\\n   claims continuing assurance. Do not leave invented or unresolved IDs.\\n6. Apply `## release_contract` or `## operating_contract` and its `### Checklist`\\n   in `docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md`.\\n7. Validate the completed draft and resolve findings within the proposed scope.\\n8. Include the contract in [Authorize the work](AUTHORIZE_WORK.md#procedure) for the exact human decision.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\nHere `TYPE` is `release_contract` or `operating_contract`, selected in action 1:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl create-artifact REPO --domain DOMAIN --type TYPE --dry-run --json\\nharnessctl create-artifact REPO --domain DOMAIN --type TYPE --id CONTRACT-ID --json\\nharnessctl validate REPO --json\\n```\\n\\n**Completion:** The applicable contract is covered by an unchanged accepted\\nrecord or a completed draft ready for its decision. Unresolved amendments\\nremain visible and block dependent work.\\n\\n**Later use:** An accepted REL governs release preparation. An accepted OPS\\ngoverns its stated continuing obligations after delivery. Perform the checks\\nand follow-up actions named in the OPS at its specified triggers; one successful\\ndelivery does not establish continuing conformance. External operating actions\\nstill require their exact authority.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"723a469b890666ae4b1e7b95a6231200a6794e6b792fef8e043ed82bc4f96ce5\"}]}, {\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\hag-context-correction34-20261011\\\\codex-291\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"71de2cc92a470e2da25d525e3ad002b77faedb6ef0e69e2fa476a2fa4cb78ff5\", \"bytes\": 11691, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"release_contract\", \"title\": \"release_contract\", \"anchor\": \"release_contract\", \"start_line\": 157, \"end_line\": 163, \"content\": \"## release_contract\\n\\n### Checklist\\n\\n- `gates` names every work order the release may include.\\n- Version, rollback conditions, and evidence expectations are explicit.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"c9c8d32b5f3c5b73f05f5d2cd120379bb50e81625a8d58d6c4d1ce25529a61f5\"}]}]}\r\n",

  "aggregated_output": "{\"resources\": [{\"resource\": \"docs/engineering/harness/RELEASE.md\", \"path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\mathi\\\\Documents\\\\Codex\\\\2026-09-20\\\\verity-plane-plugin-verity-plane-se\\\\work\\\\hag-context-correction34-20261011\\\\codex-291\\\\native\\\\inputs\\\\released-resources\\\\docs\\\\engineering\\\\harness\\\\RELEASE.md\", \"release\": {\"archive_sha256\": \"cb35c3c4eb51fe0fca575a9340b1cba6cd63b5f7133a0ebeb3fd32b4ed863053\", \"payload_sha256\": \"0e7b7c2bc10b06150c6c1ebe88d796d047f5d906bdfb5ef4e00914a56c79e7ff\", \"version\": \"0.22.1\"}, \"sha256\": \"ce700f8f764c4425978f070d978d48eacafb927601f45e298c765f46dae90f7f\", \"bytes\": 7849, \"sections\": [{\"heading\": \"before-this-action\", \"title\": \"Before this action\", \"anchor\": \"before-this-action\", \"start_line\": 7, \"end_line\": 10, \"content\": \"## Before this action\\n\\nBefore preparing, read [WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#release-coverage](WORK_AND_EVIDENCE.md#release-coverage) and the selected REL/VREC records. Before a release decision, read [AUTHORITY.md#decision-rights](AUTHORITY.md#decision-rights) and [AUTHORITY.md#delegation-and-separation](AUTHORITY.md#delegation-and-separation).\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"ddbc0b4cafdf1d5c05a185936aa8cb848c0028eeca29b9bc05ee6365782404b0\"}, {\"heading\": \"prepare-a-release-record\", \"title\": \"Prepare a release record\", \"anchor\": \"prepare-a-release-record\", \"start_line\": 13, \"end_line\": 71, \"content\": \"### Prepare a release record\\n\\n**Inputs:** The selected path, existing preparation authority, exact candidate,\\nand the release contract (REL) and eligible verified coverage required by that\\npath. Release-record preparation requires both.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Release path:** One release record (RLS) in `ready` and its generated\\n  evaluator evidence, when preparation is required and succeeds.\\n- **Retained files:** Required build or delivery evidence at the authorized\\n  locations. Builds occur only when separately covered by the selected scope.\\n- **Transient working material:** Preparation notes, proposed external content,\\n  and inspected write destinations.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Confirm authority for the exact preparation operation. Obtain a missing\\n   human decision before writing; reuse matching authority already supplied.\\n2. Inspect existing records and outputs before creating replacements.\\n3. For release, select an active release contract (REL), version, domain,\\n   and unused release record (RLS) ID. Check local Git refs and existing\\n   version reservations before choosing the ID and version.\\n4. Select the final eligible verification record (VREC) for the candidate.\\n   Its work-order (WO) set must exactly cover the work being released.\\n5. Confirm all intended output paths and the clean working-tree condition\\n   required by release preparation.\\n6. Run the release preparation command. Inspect its written record, evidence,\\n   candidate identity, and `ready` state.\\n7. Retain the new release record (RLS) and evidence in an authorized governance\\n   commit after the candidate they describe.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\nFor release preparation:\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl prepare-release REPO --id RLS-ID --release-contract REL-ID --verification-record VREC-ID --work-order WO-ID --version VERSION --owner ACTOR --domain DOMAIN --json\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact RLS-ID --json\\n```\\n\\nUse the actual preparation actor for `--owner`. Preparation does not record\\na future verification or release decision. Preserve the generated record and\\nits bound evidence without changing the recorded evidence bytes.\\n\\nRepeat `--work-order` for every released work order (WO). This evaluator requires one final verification record (VREC) covering the complete\\nrelease. Earlier records remain supporting evidence. If that coverage is\\nmissing, return to verification instead of inventing or relabelling it.\\n\\nAdd `--tag TAG` only for an explicitly selected tag value; this records the\\nvalue and does not create a Git tag. `prepare-release` writes after its checks;\\nit has no `--dry-run` or `--apply` option.\\n\\n**Completion:** The required delivery inputs are prepared, or a precise\\npreparation blocker is known. Preparation performs no merge, publication,\\ndeployment, or release decision.\\n\\n**Later use:** A ready release record (RLS) proceeds to [Obtain the release decision, when required](RELEASE.md#obtain-the-release-decision-when-required). \\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"d3fcc6f4d9565acc0d714479b8b27df0173ce927ec4d36a757bf1f5710f34942\"}, {\"heading\": \"record-the-release-decision-when-required\", \"title\": \"Record the release decision, when required\", \"anchor\": \"record-the-release-decision-when-required\", \"start_line\": 117, \"end_line\": 159, \"content\": \"### Record the release decision, when required\\n\\n**Inputs:** The human's exact decision and unchanged release inputs.\\n\\n**Output:**\\n\\n- **Formal artifacts:** Only the selected release record (RLS) receives the\\n  permitted state and lifecycle-history entry.\\n- **Retained files:** The updated release record (RLS), retained through\\n  authorized Git actions.\\n- **Transient working material:** The applied result and current next action.\\n\\n**Actions:**\\n\\n1. Compare the current release inputs with the human's reviewed inputs.\\n2. Preview the selected transition.\\n3. Apply the same command when its gates pass and effects match the decision.\\n4. Inspect the release record (RLS) and report the actual resulting state.\\n\\n**Harness commands:**\\n\\n```text\\nharnessctl transition REPO --set RLS-ID=TARGET --decision RLS-ID=ACTOR --json\\nharnessctl transition REPO --set RLS-ID=TARGET --decision RLS-ID=ACTOR --apply --json\\nharnessctl check REPO --artifact RLS-ID --json\\n```\\n\\nFor rejection, add `--reason \\\"RLS-ID=Rejection reason\\\"` to both transition\\ncommands. Related verification records (VREC) and work orders (WO) are not\\ntransitioned automatically.\\n\\nFor a complete-release decision, use the existing `--reason` input to retain the\\nactual human decision reference and reviewed delivery-plan path and SHA-256.\\nThis is retained evidence of the supplied decision, not permission derived by\\nparsing arbitrary reason text. Preserve the referenced plan bytes for each later\\nauthority comparison. No new approval file or lifecycle state is needed.\\n\\n**Completion:** The release decision is recorded or explicitly refused.\\nNo Git tag, publication, or deployment has been performed by this transition.\\n\\n**Later use:** A released record may support [Confirm authority for the external action](DELIVER_RESULT.md#confirm-authority-for-the-external-action)'s external-action checks.\\nRejection follows the evaluator's remediation procedure.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"41884593e91b2762c5d0406d1b6e73f0f7731edf06676a4cf15a64b0760c789d\"}]}]}\r\n",

Present the candidate, included work, verification coverage, version,\\n   constraints, rollback conditions, and required release evidence.\\n   If the contract and delivery plan select complete release delivery, follow\\n   [Complete-release authority](AUTHORITY.md#complete-release-authority). Finish\\n   required deliverable preparation and human verification before this request.\\n   Show one concise request: \\\"Approve the complete release\\\", its versions,\\n   delivery actions, verification summary, limitations and a link to the exact\\n   plan. Include payload digests, destinations, marker targets and any bounded\\n   release-only integration in that plan.\\n2. Run the transition gate check for the intended target state.\\n3.                                               | Result order, and assurance classification.                                       | Approval or rejection of the selected work order.                                                    |\\n| `DR-WO-START`              | Human or Agent executing the selected work under its recorded approval.                                                            | Unchanged approved scope and passing start checks.                                                                | The selected work order becomes `in_progress`.                                                       |\\n| `DR-WO-COMPLETE`           |                                               | The selected work order becomes `implemented`.                                                       |\\n| `DR-VREC-PREPARE`          | Human or Agent passing preparation checks.     | One `ready` verification record; no acceptance decision.                                             |\\n| `DR-VREC-DECIDE`           | Human authorized to accept                    | Decision on that verification record only.                                                           |\\n| `DR-DELIVERY-SELECT`       | Human authorized for the chosen integration Supplying either identity does not grant\\nauthority. The decision\\nand its resulting state MUST remain specific to the selected artifact.\\n\\n\", \"content_sha256\": \"6ecaeb29429bcaa4eac99857f2f921e270c4865d1edeec96f536d09eb6c3130a\"}, {\"heading\": \"delegation-and-separation\", \"title\": \"Delegation and separation\", \"anchor\": \"delegation-and-separation\", \"start_line\": 111, \"end_line\": 133, \"content\": \"## Delegation and separation\\n\\nA human decision right may be delegated only to another human who is permitted\\nto hold it. Typed and\\nraw input cannot be mixed. Documents are exact UTF-8 files. No manual base64 or\\ncopied client digest is needed. `--include-document` adds one read of the exact\\ncreated revision, returning text or a decoded file path. Inspect it before editing.\\n\\n`--record` retains the command. Its new `.evidence` directory retains exact\\nrequests/responses and decoded documents. The displayed `client_view` is the\\nclient's own view. Inspect outcomes and findings; read required omitted content.\\nDo not reread a whole receipt just to extract a small field already displayed.\\nA capture error after send can leave a committed effect. Reconcile its original\\nkey with `remote operation --key KEY --record ABSOLUTE_NEW_RECORD`.\\n\\n## Read one revision\\n\\n```text\\nremote read --typed --compact --record ABSOLUTE_NEW_RECORD --artifact ID --expected-revision REVISION --context UUID --context-version N\\n```\\n\\nFor an imported baseline, replace the context fields with `--baseline ID`.\\nReads take no `--operation-key`, `--expected-project-version` or `--evaluator-file`.\\nChoose the exact revision and context from the selected inputs or actual results.\\n\\n## Reads and discovery\\n\\n| Need | Operation |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| Service readiness and selected components | `remote status --record ABSOLUTE_NEW_RECORD` |\\n| Local wheel metadata | `identity` |\\n| Captured calls, reads and failures so far | `observations --record ABSOLUTE_NEW_RECORD`; retains the full snapshot and returns its field pointers, no content verdict |\\n| Complete released instruction sections | `instructions --section \\\"RESOURCE_ID#HEADING\\\"`; repeat for up to 12 sections |\\n| One unknown input location | `find-file BASENAME --under RELATIVE_DIRECTORY/` |\\n| One exact inventory entry | `lookup-file RELATIVE_NAME` |\\n| One saved JSON field | `read-json ABSOLUTE_FILE --pointer '\\\"/field\\\"'`; omit pointer for root; optional `--keys` |\\n| A raw base64 field | Add `--decode-base64` to that field read |\\n| One text file or independent reads together | `read-text ABSOLUTE_FILE [ABSOLUTE_FILE ...]`; up to eight selected inventoried inputs, the launcher-pinned task.md, or work files, at most 64 KiB output |\\n| Recover a truncated text read | `read-text ABSOLUTE_FILE --offset 0 --limit 4096`; one file, character offsets; continue from next_offset until complete is true |\\n\\nFor `instructions`, use canonical IDs such as `docs/engineering/harness/DRAFT_DEFINITIONS.md#read-this-when`. The earlier `released-resources/` inventory prefix also works. Request known sections together.\\nFor authoring checklists and the repeated released 0.22.1 continuation heading,\\nuse the exact selectors in the selected plugin's `change/references/hosted-drafts.md`.\\n\\nFor known paths, use them directly. Inventory names are relative to the staged\\ninputs directory: `released-resources/docs/engineering/ARTIFACT_AUTHORING.md`,\\n`source/src/greeting.py`, `client-help/create-artifact.txt`. **Do not add `inputs/`\\nto these names.** Native Read takes the absolute path, not an inventory name.\\nA digest or lookup is not a content read. Batch independent reads when their exact\\npaths are known. Unknown headings must not be guessed;\\nread the named file once to locate its actual headings. Missing\\nreads remain unknown; rereading now does not prove an earlier read. The capture\\nmay be incomplete, and subsequent report writes are not yet counted. Keep the\\nrecord path as evidence instead of copying every command. This supplies no draft\\ntext, content judgement or lifecycle decision.\\n\\n`command_records` includes extensionless record names.
